cl_avfx_preset0=off / 1=rain / 2=snow / 3=ash / 4=dust / 5=mistAtmospheric preset selector. 0=off, 1=rain (RF_BEAM streaks + optional close raindrop particles + optional storm), 2=snow (white drifting particles), 3=ash (orange/grey motes for lava/industrial maps), 4=dust (tan/grey low-alpha motes), 5=mist (very-low-alpha large slow particles — not a fog substitute, layers over usefog).
cl_avfx_puddle_step_splash_amount0..5 (default 1.0)Intensity multiplier for puddle step splashes, 0..5. 1.0 is the default visual. 0 disables the visible foot splashes while keeping puddle step audio active. Higher values add more droplets and slightly stronger spread, but the effect still requires run speed and visible puddle coverage.
cl_avfx_puddle_step_splashes0=off / 1=on (default)Visual splash particles when the local player runs through visible AVFX puddles. Slow walking keeps only wet step audio; jog/run speed throws a small silent burst from the foot contact point. The effect is gated by the same visible-puddle coverage used by puddle step sounds, so hidden runoff/helper state never creates visual splashes on dry-looking floor.
cl_avfx_quality0=low / 1=normal (default) / 2=highPer-frame budget tier. low=48 rain beams + 80 particles, normal=96+160, high=160+280. Competitive limit clamps these further during multiplayer. AVFX never evicts gameplay visuals; emission is late in CL_AddEntities and only fills leftover MAX_ENTITIES / MAX_PARTICLES headroom.
cl_avfx_radius128..2048 (default 768)Horizontal radius (in world units) of the camera-local weather volume. Particles / beams are deterministically distributed inside this square around cl.refdef.vieworg.
cl_avfx_rain_drop_density0.0..1.0 (default 0.35)Density of the close raindrop layer (independent of main streak density). Multiplied by cl_avfx_weather_level. Only effective when cl_avfx_rain_drops=1 and the rain preset is active.
cl_avfx_rain_drop_shape0.0..3.0 (default 1.0)Close-raindrop elongation. 0 = round/legacy-like sprite (old V_AddParticle look); 1 = default short wind-aligned mini-streak matching the main rain streaks; values above 1 lengthen the close streaks toward cinematic. Shape/length only, not density. Direction follows cl_avfx_wind_x / cl_avfx_wind_y exactly like the main rain.
cl_avfx_rain_drop_size0.05..1.0 (default 0.25)Visual size multiplier applied ONLY to close-drop sprites/mini-streaks (does not touch the main rain streak size — those still use cl_avfx_size directly). Default 0.25 keeps close drops visually smaller than the main rain curtain so the two layers do not blend.
cl_avfx_rain_drops0=disable close drops / 1=enable close drops (default)Enable the close raindrop detail particle layer when the rain preset is active. Adds a small population of near-camera particles standing in for splashes / spray. Only meaningful for cl_avfx_preset=1.
cl_avfx_rain_flow_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=overlay (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: visualizes the AVFX rain flow/runoff field. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_avfx_rain_flow_debug_alphadefault 0.75 / range 0..1 (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: opacity of the rain-flow debug overlay. Only affects the overlay when cl_avfx_rain_flow_debug is on.
cl_avfx_rain_flow_debug_radiusdefault 8192 / world units (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: world-space radius of the rain-flow debug overlay. Only affects the overlay when cl_avfx_rain_flow_debug is on.
cl_avfx_rain_gpu0=legacy RF_BEAM streaks / 1=GPU streak pass (default)Use the GPU rain-streak pass instead of the legacy per-streak entity path. This is a kill switch: when it is off, or when the weather renderer is Classic, or when the hardware cannot run the pass, Q2PRO-X falls back to the legacy RF_BEAM streaks automatically and rain stays visible either way. Requires cl_avfx 1 and the rain preset (cl_avfx_preset 1).
cl_avfx_rain_on_eyes0=off (default) / 1=onOptional rain-on-eyes / wet-lens postprocess while the player stands under open-sky rain. It uses non-uniform screen-space blur, misty soft patches and a faint wet tint rather than drawing more rain particles. Off by default for clear visibility. It disappears under roofs, underwater, and outside the rain preset. In competitive-limited multiplayer the intensity is automatically reduced.
cl_avfx_rain_on_eyes_amount0..1 (default 0.65)Wet-lens blur / misting intensity, 0..1. 0 disables the effect even if the master toggle is on; 0.65 is the default. The final strength also scales with cl_avfx_density and cl_avfx_weather_level, so light rain stays subtle and heavy rain looks wetter.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_alpha0..1 (default 0.4)Puddle opacity multiplier. Lower values keep the floor texture more visible; higher values make accumulated water read darker and wetter. Applies to generated AVFX puddle decals and their flow continuation.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_cascade_field_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=overlay (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: visualizes the AVFX puddle cascade/flow field. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_cascade_field_density0.1..3 (default 1)Multiplier on how much water each cascade deposit adds to the puddle cascade field. Higher values fill lower puddles faster and make cascades read as heavier; lower values keep the lower level drier for longer. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_rain_puddles 1 with cascades active.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_count0.2..500 (default 1.0)Concurrent puddle budget multiplier. Controls how many generated puddles/flow pieces may live at once before the pool starts reusing old entries. Visual presets scale this together with puddle size and LOD.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_density0..1 (default 1.0)Fraction of qualifying horizontal rain hits that spawn a puddle decal, 0..1. 1.0 (default) — every horizontal hit gets a puddle (capped by AVFX_DECAL_MAX = 384 active decals shared with snow caps). 0.5 — roughly half. 0.0 — disabled (same as cl_avfx_rain_puddles 0). Lowering density reduces overlap density — rare hits read as scattered dark spots; high density saturates the visible floor.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_dust0..3 (default 1.0)Amount of drifting dark dirt particles inside puddles. Sloped puddles push particles along the water direction; flat puddles use subtle chaotic drift. 0 disables puddle debris.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_dust_size0.1..3.0 (default 1.0)Size multiplier for visible dirt/debris particles inside puddles and related flow areas. Does not change particle count, only their visual scale.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_fill_rate0.01..20.0 (default 0.2)Puddle fill/growth speed multiplier. Values below 1 make puddles appear and spread more slowly; values above 1 make wet surfaces fill faster. Used by direct rain puddles and downstream water-flow growth.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_max_size0.2..100.0 (default 1.0)Puddle max-size multiplier. Ultra Quality can use large values for broad natural wet areas; performance presets reduce it so puddles stay smaller and cheaper while still growing normally.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection0/1 (default 0)Master toggle for MODEL reflections in rain puddles. When on, the per-category toggles below (weapons / armor / items / players+monsters / ships / meteors / comets / planets) choose what reflects. All categories default OFF, so this alone does nothing until at least one is enabled.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_actors0/1 (default 0)Reflect player and monster models in rain puddles. Needs the puddle MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_armor0/1 (default 0)Reflect armor models in rain puddles. Needs the puddle MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_comets0/1 (default 0)Reflect AVFX comets in rain puddles. Needs the puddle MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_items0/1 (default 0)Reflect item / object models in rain puddles. Needs the puddle MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_meteors0/1 (default 0)Reflect AVFX sky meteors (shooting-star streaks + embers) in rain puddles. Needs the puddle MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_planets0/1 (default 0)Reflect the AVFX Earth, Moon, Sun, Black Hole and compatible celestial bodies in rain puddles (per-pixel reflected-ray disk + a spatial BSP line-of-sight mask, with corona glow). Needs AVFX world on and rain puddles present; independent of the model-reflection master. Each body also needs its own master enabled, so this category plus cl_avfx_blackhole is the complete gate for the Black Hole — there is deliberately no separate black-hole reflection toggle. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_projectiles0/1 (default 0)Reflect final presented projectiles and the rail beam in rain puddles, including synchronized local prediction. Needs the puddle model-reflection master. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_ships0/1 (default 0)Reflect AVFX sky spaceships in rain puddles. Needs the puddle MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_strength0..1 (default 0.8)Strength / opacity of model reflections in rain puddles.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_surface_volumes0/1 (default 0)Reflect placed Surface Volumes (steam, smoke and fog) in rain puddles. Needs the puddle model-reflection master. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_model_reflection_weapons0/1 (default 0)Reflect weapon models in rain puddles. Needs the puddle MODEL-reflection master on. Default OFF.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_reflection_distort0..1 (default 0)Liquid distortion of ALL puddle reflections (SSR + models + sky objects): warps the reflection like moving liquid with uneven travelling ripples, scaled by the puddle surface speed. 0 = sharp mirror.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_reflection_distort_speed0..5 (default 1)Speed of the puddle reflection ripple. 1 = default, 0 = frozen ripple.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_rings0=off / 1=on (default)Puddle-surface rings. When rain or water contacts an already wet AVFX puddle, the renderer emits flat expanding rings on the puddle plane. Does not affect true water-surface rain rings.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff0=off / 1=on (default)Water runoff from puddle edges. Allows accumulated puddles to continue as visible water flow over steps, ledges and lower connected surfaces. Ultra Performance may disable it, all higher presets keep it enabled.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff_dust0..3 (default 1.0)Amount of dark debris/dirt particles moving inside puddle runoff streams. 0 disables the debris layer; higher values make flow direction easier to read.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff_dynamics0..1 (default 0.75)Temporal life of organic runoff strands (style 1): how strongly individual strands start, grow, thin out, stop, and get replaced by nearby new strands over time. Stays deterministic (no frame-to-frame noise flicker). Higher = more visible change over time.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff_grow_speed0.05..10.0 (default 0.2)Runoff visual extension speed multiplier. Low values make streams visibly crawl from the source puddle; high values make them reach the lower surface quickly.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff_lod0=Full / 1=Follow LOD / 2=Near (default 1)LOD mode for puddle runoff CPU simulation/rendering. Full ignores runoff LOD; Follow uses Distance LOD only when it is enabled. Near keeps runoff near the camera even when Distance LOD is off. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_rain_puddles 1 + cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff 1. Full keeps every runoff stream simulated regardless of distance, so it is the most expensive setting.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff_scale0.1..5.0 (default 1.0)Global runoff stream thickness multiplier. Scales the visual width of water streams generated from puddle edges, on top of per-stream randomization and source puddle size.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff_specular0..1 (default 0.60)Strength of small wet highlights along organic runoff strands (style 1).
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff_style0 classic, 1 organic (default 0)Runoff renderer for water flowing from puddle edges. 0 = classic (the existing flat-strip renderer, unchanged). 1 = organic: multiple irregular strands per stream with varied width, broken segments, uneven alpha, subtle world-space wobble, small wet specular highlights, and temporal life (strands start, grow, thin, end, and nearby strands appear asynchronously). The runoff simulation/lifecycle is shared; only the look changes. Default 0.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_runoff_variation0..1 (default 0.70)Strand count, irregularity and breakup variation for organic runoff (style 1). Higher = more varied, more broken strands.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_scene_reflection0/1 (default 0)Screen-space reflection (SSR) of nearby world geometry in rain puddles. Reflects only what is on screen (marches a few hundred units); MODEL and sky-object reflections are separate toggles below.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_scene_reflection_qualitylow / medium / highPuddle SSR quality (march step count / resolution). Higher = smoother, sharper reflection at more GPU cost.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_scene_reflection_strength0..1Strength / opacity of the puddle SSR reflection.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_specular0=off / 1=on (default)Fake wet specular shimmer on AVFX puddles. Adds moving highlights and a small sky-tint mix so wet surfaces read as water rather than just dark stains.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_specular_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=overlay (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: visualizes AVFX puddle specular/reflection terms. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_specular_strength0..1 (default 0.6)Intensity multiplier for fake puddle specular highlights. 0 keeps puddles matte; 1 gives the strongest shimmer allowed by the shader.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_surface_objects0/1 (default 1)Reflect enabled grass, ivy, ferns and falling leaves in puddles. Stones, soil and ground litter are excluded before mesh work. Uses scene reflection strength; does not enable objects themselves.
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_surface_speed0.1..10 (default 1.0)AVFX puddle style motion speed multiplier. 1.0 (default) = baseline; 0.1 = 10x slower, 10 = 10x faster. Scales puddle film/dirt motion. No effect at style 0 (Standard).
cl_avfx_rain_puddle_surface_style0..12 (default 0)AVFX puddle surface material style. 0 = Standard (exact current look, no style texture). 1..12 = reference-derived puddle tiles (wet asphalt, muddy, swamp film, droplets, clean wet floor, foam, etc.) at pics/q2prox/avfx/ps/. Mask/DETAIL only inside the existing puddle alpha — breaks up wetness/dirt/film/specular; never determines whether a puddle exists and does NOT gate any AVFX puddle effect (rings, runoff, dust, step splashes, reflection, celestial/lightning). Live, no vid_restart; missing tile falls back to Standard.
cl_avfx_rain_puddles0=no puddles / 1=puddles (default)Wet-patch puddle decals where rain hits horizontal hard surfaces. Each rain hit on a floor / table-top (surface normal.z > 0.7) optionally spawns a translucent dark blue-grey patch that grows briefly, holds, then fades over ~6-12 seconds. Continued rain refreshes the visual via fresh overlapping spawns. 0 — no puddles. 1 (default) — enable. Cleared on level change; never written to map data.
cl_avfx_rain_realistic0/1 (default 0 = legacy main rain)Switch the MAIN / background rain streaks (not close drops) from the legacy uniform style to a realistic style: irregular, wind-slanted, tapered streaks with a thin/darker upstream tail and a brighter/thicker rounded downstream head that follows the rain+wind direction. Two controlled shape families — the rounded-head drop-streak and a rarer line-like streak (see cl_avfx_rain_realistic_line_mix). Default 0 (legacy). Does NOT replace close drops (cl_avfx_rain_drops).
cl_avfx_rain_realistic_amount0.1..20 (default 5)Count multiplier for realistic MAIN rain streaks (PO Bugs/66). The realistic field was density-limited, so this scales how dense the streak grid is: 1.0 = the old realistic amount, 5.0 (default) = ~5x more drops, up to 20 = ~20x more, down to 0.1 = ~10x fewer. Only used when cl_avfx_rain_realistic 1. Bounded by the entity budget at the high end.
cl_avfx_rain_realistic_depth0..1 (default 0.60)Depth-layer attenuation and distance variation for the realistic main rain field (nearer streaks stronger, farther dimmer/thinner). Only used when cl_avfx_rain_realistic 1.
cl_avfx_rain_realistic_head_bias0..1 (default 0.70)Strength of the brighter/thicker rounded downstream head on realistic main rain streaks — the main reference look where the lower/downstream end is a small lit water mass. The head follows the actual rain fall direction including wind slant (never hard-coded screen-down). Only used when cl_avfx_rain_realistic 1.
cl_avfx_rain_realistic_line_mix0..1 (default 0.20)Share of the secondary line-like streak family in realistic main rain. 0 = mostly rounded-head drop-streaks; higher adds more elongated line streaks (still with non-uniform center-bright / edge-dark shading, not uniform rods). Only used when cl_avfx_rain_realistic 1.
cl_avfx_rain_realistic_softness0..1 (default 0.65)Edge softness / taper of realistic main rain streaks. Higher makes streaks less rod-like and more tapered. Only used when cl_avfx_rain_realistic 1.
cl_avfx_rain_realistic_variation0..1 (default 0.75)Per-streak variation of length, width, opacity and brightness for realistic main rain. Higher = more diverse streaks. Only used when cl_avfx_rain_realistic 1.
cl_avfx_rain_ripple_alpha0..1 (menu step 0.05, default 1)Opacity of rain rings on standard BSP water (0..1, default 1.0). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples 1; rings spawn only on sky-exposed water and are subject to the per-frame ring budget.
cl_avfx_rain_ripple_density0..1 (default 1.0)Fraction of would-be water hits that spawn ring impacts, 0..1. 1.0 (default) spawns a ring burst per drop hit (every drop produces rings); 0.5 thins to roughly half; 0.0 disables ring spawning entirely (same effect as cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples 0). Each main rain drop spawns a 3-ring chase sequence; close drops spawn a single smaller ring. Per-ring radius / strength / lifetime are randomized so concurrent drops don't expand in lock-step.
cl_avfx_rain_ripple_impact_density0..1 (menu step 0.05, default 0.35)Fraction of rain rings that show a drop/impact dot at the centre (0..1, default 0.35). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples 1; rings spawn only on sky-exposed water and are subject to the per-frame ring budget.
cl_avfx_rain_ripple_roundness0..3 (menu step 1, default 1)Roundness of rain rings on standard BSP water: 0 = coarse/cheaper, 1 = standard, 2 = smooth, 3 = ultra-smooth. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples 1; rings spawn only on sky-exposed water and are subject to the per-frame ring budget.
cl_avfx_rain_ripple_speed0.1..3.0 (default 1.0; <1 = slower / softer; >1 = faster / sharper)Ring expansion / fade speed multiplier, 0.1..3.0. 1.0 (default) keeps the original cadence (rings expand and fade across roughly 480-820 ms with a 130-190 ms stagger between the 3 chase rings of one burst). 0.1 stretches everything 10x — rings grow and dissolve very gently, ~5-8 seconds per ring. 3.0 compresses everything 3x — rings expand and fade in ~160-280 ms, snappier splashes. Lifetime AND inter-ring stagger both scale, so the burst chase relationship stays proportional at every speed.
cl_avfx_rain_ripple_stroke0.25..3 (menu step 0.05, default 1)Stroke width of the ring outline on standard BSP water. 1.0 = current look; lower = thinner, higher = thicker. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples 1; rings spawn only on sky-exposed water and are subject to the per-frame ring budget.
cl_avfx_rain_splash_density0..1 (default 1.0)Fraction of would-be hard-surface rain hits that spawn splash bursts, 0..1. 1.0 (default) spawns a splash on every qualifying hit; 0.5 thins to roughly half; 0.0 disables splash spawning entirely (same effect as cl_avfx_rain_splashes 0). Splash slot buffer caps active splashes at AVFX_SPLASH_MAX = 128 — heavy density just saturates faster, never exceeds the cap, so the per-frame work stays bounded.
cl_avfx_rain_splash_scale0.2..5.0 (default 1.0; <1 = smaller / softer; >1 = larger / heavier)Splash burst SIZE multiplier, 0.2..5.0. 1.0 (default) keeps the original tuning (subtle 5-droplet bursts that arc ~30 units up and ~12 units out). 0.2 shrinks everything 5× — barely-visible micro-droplets, suitable for light drizzle. 5.0 enlarges everything 5× — heavy splashes with droplets arcing several feet, suitable for storm rain. Scale is applied to particle size, horizontal spread radius, vertical launch speed, AND the virtual-gravity term so the trajectory shape stays proportional at every setting.
cl_avfx_rain_splashes0=no splashes / 1=splashes (default)Rain splash bursts on hard surfaces. Each rain spawn point that traces down to a non-liquid surface (not water / lava / slime / sky) produces a small upward burst of light-blue droplet particles that arc parabolically and fade out over ~250-400 ms. Independent of cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples (water hits → rings; hard hits → splashes). Both events come from the same per-frame trace pass so the work scales with whichever density cvar is higher. 0 — disable splashes. 1 (default) — enable.
cl_avfx_rain_water_contact0=off / 1=on (default)Rain/water contact layer on true water surfaces. Enables rain rings, small bubbles/foam and related surface interaction when weather hits CONTENTS_WATER. Lava and slime use separate steam handling.
cl_avfx_rain_water_contact_bubble_density0..1 (default 0.65)Density multiplier for rain-contact bubbles/foam on true water surfaces.
cl_avfx_rain_water_contact_bubble_size0.2..5.0 (default 1.0)Size multiplier for rain-contact bubbles/foam on true water surfaces.
cl_avfx_rain_water_contact_bubbles0=off / 1=on (default)Small drifting bubbles/foam on true water contacts. This is separate from puddle debris and from the enhanced-water foam shader.
cl_avfx_rain_water_contact_ripple_alpha0..1 (menu step 0.05, default 1)Opacity of water-contact rings from runoff and water-to-water contact (0..1, default 1.0). Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples 1; it affects only the contact/runoff rings, not the rain-impact rings.
cl_avfx_rain_water_contact_ripple_roundness0..3 (menu step 1, default 1)Roundness of water-contact rings: 0 = coarse/cheaper, 1 = standard, 2 = smooth, 3 = ultra-smooth. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples 1; it affects only the contact/runoff rings, not the rain-impact rings.
cl_avfx_rain_water_contact_ripple_stroke0.25..3 (menu step 0.05, default 1)Stroke width of the water-contact rings. 1.0 = current look; lower = thinner, higher = thicker. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples 1; it affects only the contact/runoff rings, not the rain-impact rings.
cl_avfx_rain_water_ripples0=no water ripples / 1=allow ripples (default)Allow expanding ring impacts on water surfaces when rain hits them. An independent SPAWN pass samples a disc around the camera, traces with MASK_SOLID/MASK_WATER and spawns a 3-ring burst on each water hit (R3: when the camera is underwater the trace start is automatically lifted above the local water ceiling so rings still spawn on the surface above). Each visible ring renders as a fixed 16-chord RF_BEAM polygon (smooth circle silhouette). The per-frame entity budget caps how many rings render so storm / lightning bolts (which run after rings) keep their reserve; surplus rings beyond the cap are skipped entirely and counted in cl_avfx_info ripple skip stats (R5). Independent of cl_avfx_water (water visual master) — ripples can be on without the water shader. Subject to cl_avfx_world gate (R1) and open-sky exposure (R2 — no rings under indoor roofs).
cl_avfx_render_lod0..1 (default 1)Master toggle for distance LOD culling of small AVFX effects (foam bubbles, water ripples, puddle rings, splashes, puddle dust, snow caps, snow blanket cells). Soft fade over the last 30% of cl_avfx_render_lod_wu range. Particle spawn radius is also clamped by lod_wu so CPU work scales with the LOD distance — set lod_wu < cl_avfx_radius for real fps gain. Surface decals (puddles), cascade flow paths, and rain particles themselves are NEVER culled.
cl_avfx_render_lod_wu256..4096 (default 1536)Distance threshold in world units beyond which LOD-culled effects are no longer rendered. Values below cl_avfx_radius (default 768) actually shrink the spawn cylinder, saving CPU. Values above only fade alpha at the visual edge. Default 1536 = visual edge well outside spawn cylinder, no spawn cull at default radius.
cl_avfx_size0.25..4.0 (default 1.0)Size multiplier for streaks / particles. Affects rain streak length and beam diameter, snow/ash/dust/mist particle scale.
cl_avfx_sky0=map sky / 1=weather (default) / 2=blue skySky rendering mode (3-way). 0 = Map sky: the map's own sky texture, no AVFX sky. 1 = Weather sky (default): AVFX weather-driven sky tint, procedural cloud overlay and weather fog on sky surfaces (couples to rain/snow profiles via cl_avfx_sky_auto/override_mode/clouds). 2 = Blue sky: procedural blue daytime sky (the Summer Blue Sky look; tuned by cl_avfx_sky_blue_intensity/saturation/horizon_fade/...). Modes are mutually exclusive.
cl_avfx_sky_auto0=manual / 1=auto-coupled (default)Auto-couple sky look to the active weather strength. Heavier weather can darken the sky and increase clouds/fog; manual values remain the baseline.
cl_avfx_sky_blue_cloud_preservedefault 1.0 / range 0.0..1.0 / step 0.05Keep the procedural cloud overlay visible over the blue sky (Blue sky mode). 1.0 = default (clouds preserved); 0 = blue sky hides them.
cl_avfx_sky_blue_horizon_fadedefault 0.45 / range 0.0..1.0 / step 0.05Blue-sky fade toward the horizon (Blue sky mode). 0.45 = default; higher lightens the horizon band.
cl_avfx_sky_blue_intensitydefault 1.0 / range 0.0..3.0 / step 0.05Blue-sky colour intensity (Blue sky mode, cl_avfx_sky 2). 1.0 = default; higher = deeper blue.
cl_avfx_sky_blue_saturationdefault 1.0 / range 0.0..2.0 / step 0.05Blue-sky colour saturation (Blue sky mode). 1.0 = default.
cl_avfx_sky_blue_storm_morphdefault 1.0 / range 0.0..1.0 / step 0.05Morph the blue sky toward a storm tint when a storm is active (Blue sky mode). 1.0 = default; 0 keeps the blue sky unchanged during storms.
cl_avfx_sky_cloud_intensity0..1 (default 0.35)Cloud overlay intensity/density. Higher values make clouds more visible and the sky visually heavier.
cl_avfx_sky_cloud_speed0..4 (default 2.1)Cloud drift speed multiplier. 0 freezes the cloud layer; higher values make the overlay move faster across the sky.
cl_avfx_sky_clouds0=off / 1=on (default)Enable the procedural cloud overlay on sky surfaces. Cloud darkness, density and speed are controlled by the companion cloud cvars.
cl_avfx_sky_darkness0..1 (default 0.8)Base sky darkening amount used by rain/snow presets. Higher values make the sky feel heavier and more overcast.
cl_avfx_sky_fog_alpha0..1 (default 0.35)Weather fog opacity around and below the cloud layer. Helps rain/snow skies feel deeper without touching gameplay fog cvars.
cl_avfx_sky_override_mode0=off / 1=tint / 2=tint+clouds / 3=reservedWeather sky render mode. 0 disables override, 1 tints the existing sky, 2 adds tint plus cloud overlay, 3 is reserved for future replacement mode.
cl_avfx_sky_procedural_brightness0=off (default) / 1=onOpt-in procedural sky brightness driven by current sun + moon illumination. OFF (default) keeps the accepted AVFX sky look unchanged — sky color is the same regardless of where the sun/moon are. ON makes sky brightness EMERGE from the celestial state: night with no moon → sky goes fully black (there is no light source for the sky to reflect); moon at night → dim cool tint; sun above horizon → baseline brightness with mild warm bias. There is intentionally no separate darkness knob — the dark is a CONSEQUENCE of no illumination source, not a value you dial. Pair with cl_avfx_sun / cl_avfx_moon + a cycle/clock mode for live-changing sky. Independent from cl_avfx_sun_lighting / cl_avfx_moon_lighting (those gate world/entity contributions, not sky body visibility).
cl_avfx_sky_storm_tint0..1 (default 0.70)Storm mood tint amount. Adds a colder storm-colour bias on top of sky darkening when storm visuals are active.
cl_avfx_snow_accum0=no snow caps / 1=accumulate (default)Snow-cap accumulation decals where snow particles would land on horizontal hard surfaces. Each snow spawn point that traces down to a sky-exposed floor (surface normal.z > 0.7, not sky / not warp, R2 open-sky check) optionally spawns a translucent white patch that grows briefly to its target size and HOLDS while the snow preset stays active (R4: no time-fade while snow preset is on — caps persist as long as snow keeps falling). 0 — no accumulation. 1 (default) — enable. Caps clear on map change, preset switch away from snow, cl_avfx_world flip, or cl_avfx_defaults.
cl_avfx_snow_accum_alpha0..1 (default 1.0)Opacity multiplier for legacy snow cap overlays. GPU material snow uses its own shader coverage but this still affects fallback/overlay snow caps.
cl_avfx_snow_accum_count0.2..500 (default 500)Concurrent legacy snow-cap budget multiplier. Higher values allow more individual caps before the pool reuses old entries.
cl_avfx_snow_accum_density0..1 (default 1.0)Fraction of qualifying snow-spawn-on-horizontal hits that spawn a snow-cap decal, 0..1. 1.0 (default) — every qualifying hit (capped by AVFX_DECAL_MAX = 384 shared with puddles). 0.5 — roughly half (sparse caps reading as patches). 0.0 — disabled. Caps share the same buffer as puddles, so a busy rain map and a busy snow map both compete for the 384-slot pool — first-come, first-served until slots free.
cl_avfx_snow_accum_fill_rate0.01..3.00 (default 0.06)Snow accumulation fill-speed multiplier. Lower values make surfaces whiten slowly; higher values fill them faster. Capped at 3.0 because high-density snow already fills very quickly around 1.0. Also feeds footprint and weapon-mark refill logic.
cl_avfx_snow_accum_max_size0.04..4.0 (default 4.0)Maximum size multiplier for legacy snow cap overlays. Kept for fallback caps and compatibility with older snow-cover paths.
cl_avfx_snow_celestial_glitter_scaledefault 1.00 / range 0..2 / step 0.05Multiplier for snow glitter / sparkle response to celestial light. The GPU snow material's per-pixel sparkle is naturally scaled by the snow brightness scalar (length(snow_rgb) / sqrt(3)), so moonless night snow loses sparkle and noon snow retains the full accepted look. This cvar tunes that base relationship: 1.0 (default) = use the brightness scalar as-is; 0 = no celestial glitter modulation (sparkle never fades with night); up to 2.0 = sparkle exaggerated during the day, drops fast at night.
cl_avfx_snow_celestial_lighting0=off / 1=on (default)Master toggle for snow celestial lighting response. When ON (default), all visible snow paths — GPU snow material on surfaces, snow caps / snow blanket / volume extrusion overlays, 3D snowflakes, and ordinary AVFX snow flakes — react to the accepted celestial state. At noon snow stays close to the accepted bright white look; at sunrise/sunset it picks up a mild warm tint; at moonlit night it becomes dim and cold; at moonless night it darkens strongly to a deep cold tint near the minimum brightness floor. When OFF, snow returns to the fixed bright-white behavior regardless of sun/moon state. Independent from cl_avfx_sun_lighting / cl_avfx_moon_lighting — those gate world/entity contributions, while this one only re-lights the snow visuals. Requires cl_avfx 1 and a snow-enabled preset (or any snow visual currently active).
cl_avfx_snow_celestial_min_brightnessdefault 0.08 / range 0..1 / step 0.01Minimum snow brightness floor when there is no celestial light. Without this floor, moonless deep-night snow would fall to nearly black and become invisible — visually wrong for snow surfaces which are highly reflective and should still read against the world. 0.08 (default) keeps moonless snow as a deep cold dim tint, not pure black. 0 = no floor (snow goes fully dark when celestial light disappears). Higher values keep snow visibly bright even at night (less convincing).
cl_avfx_snow_celestial_night_tintdefault 0.45 / range 0..1 / step 0.05How much cold blue-grey tint the snow picks up in low-light conditions. 0.45 (default) gives a natural cold mood for moonlit / moonless snow without making daytime snow blue. The night tint is applied via mix(snow_rgb, snow_rgb × cold_color (0.55,0.62,0.78), (1 − max_light) × this). 0 = no cold tint (snow stays the same chromaticity dark as the celestial source). 1 = strongest cold push (snow reads very blue-grey in shadow).
cl_avfx_snow_celestial_strengthdefault 1.20 / range 0..2 / step 0.05How strongly celestial sun + moon illumination drives snow color/brightness. 1.20 (default) makes noon snow land near identity (very close to the accepted bright-white look) and produces a meaningful dim/cold response at night. 0 = snow color is driven entirely by the minimum brightness floor and night tint (no sun/moon influence — looks pre-baked). Up to 2.0 = strong reaction to sun/moon state. This is the artistic knob on top of the physically-emergent formula base + strength × (sun_part + moon_part).
cl_avfx_snow_dlight_headroomdefault 1.00 / range 0..1 / step 0.05 / lying snow onlyExtends the same existing-light headroom anti-washout to DYNAMIC light on LYING SNOW (TZ 2026-06-05, PO Bugs/61). Projectile dynamic lights (blaster / hyperblaster / rocket), weapon impact flashes, explosions and meteor-impact bursts all add a V_AddLight dlight; over snow that is already bright this drove the legacy lift to a flat white blob. This gate engages the same relief-preserving compressed path the flashlight uses, scaled by how bright the snow ALREADY is: dark snow still lights up fully (the dlight should), bright snow rolls off toward the luma ceiling with relief kept. Reuses the _luma_ceiling / _headroom_response / _detail_preserve / _gain / _soft_knee / _white_preserve tuning. 0 = legacy white blob (A/B); 1 (default) = full anti-washout. Lying snow only — non-snow materials and the flashlight path are unaffected. Applies to BOTH snow shader paths (GLS_AVFX_SNOW + the GPU snow material overlay).
cl_avfx_snow_field0=caps / 1=blanketLegacy uniform snow blanket toggle. 0 uses individual cap-style fallback; 1 uses the older surface-field blanket path. Modern presets primarily rely on the GPU snow material.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d0=disabled / 1=enable 3D flake batch under snow preset (default)3D snow flake batch. When 1, world-oriented quad flakes render alongside the regular particle_t snow under the SNOW preset (cl_avfx_preset 2). Flake basis is computed at spawn and stays anchored to world space — looking around shows flakes at varying angles instead of always face-on. Default 1 for the accepted snow profile parameters. Does not consume entity_t or particle_t budget — uses a separate 800-slot pool (v2) with its own batched draw call after particles.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_count0.2..2.0 (default 2.0)flake density multiplier. Multiplies the v2 base target of 440 active flakes by this value, clamped to the pool cap of 800. 0.2 ≈ 88 flakes (sparse), 1.0 = base 440, 2.0 = clamped 800. Range 0.2..2.0. Use this to tune perceived density without changing AVFX weather level / preset. This cvar multiplies the selected 3D snow preset density, so it remains effective even when cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_quality is non-zero.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_crossed0=single quad / 1=crossed quads (default)crossed-quads mode. 1 (default) renders each 3D flake as TWO perpendicular quads (the original axis_u/axis_v plane plus a second quad in the axis_v/axis_w plane where axis_w = axis_u × axis_v). Eliminates edge-on slivers — there is no single view direction where both quads collapse to a line, so flakes always read as proper volumetric specks instead of disappearing at certain angles. Costs 2× vertex bandwidth per flake (12 verts vs 6). 0 = single-quad v1 mode (cheaper; some flakes appear as thin slivers when viewed near edge-on). Effective only when cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d is on. When cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_quality is non-zero this cvar is overridden by the preset.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal0=Off / 1=On (default 0)Replace round 3D snowflakes with real 6-armed fractal snowflake shapes from a generated atlas. Optional; OFF keeps the accepted round flakes. Same lighting as ordinary snow. Requires cl_avfx 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d 1. Turning it on builds a runtime snowflake atlas once (forms x tile resolution of texture memory); the flakes themselves cost the same as the round ones.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal_forms4..64 (menu step 1, default 16)Number of unique snowflake shapes in the atlas (4..64). More = less repetition, slightly more atlas memory. Requires cl_avfx 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2), cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d 1 and cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal 1.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal_max_size1..64 (menu step 0.5, default 14)Absolute maximum flake half-size in world units (caps giant flakes). Requires cl_avfx 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2), cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d 1 and cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal 1.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal_size_max0.1..6 (menu step 0.05, default 1.75)Maximum size multiplier (relative to the base flake size) for fractal flakes. Requires cl_avfx 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2), cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d 1 and cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal 1.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal_size_min0.1..4 (menu step 0.05, default 0.75)Minimum size multiplier (relative to the base flake size) for fractal flakes. Requires cl_avfx 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2), cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d 1 and cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal 1.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal_tile0=64 / 1=128 / 2=256 (default 1)Atlas tile resolution (quality vs memory). 256 = crispest, 64 = lightest. Requires cl_avfx 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2), cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d 1 and cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_fractal 1.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_near0.1..1.0 (default 1.0; lower = more LOD, less cost)near-radius LOD gate. Fraction of the spawn radius within which 3D flakes render as crossed quads; flakes farther from the camera than (spawn_radius * this_value) keep marching in the pool but skip the 3D submit, so the cheaper particle_t snow path carries them visually at distance. 1.0 (default) disables LOD — every alive flake submits as 3D. 0.6 ≈ 64% area saving on vertex bandwidth at default spawn. 0.1 = aggressive (only the very closest flakes render as 3D; rest drop to particle_t). Useful for tuning frame cost on weaker GPUs / dense weather without losing apparent snow density. Telemetry: the developer 1 log line avfx_flakes_3d: shows submitted vs lod_skipped counts every second. Effective only when cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d is on. When cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_quality is non-zero this cvar is overridden by the preset.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_quality0=manual / 1=performance / 2=balanced / 3=rich (default)3D-flake quality preset. Convenience selector for crossed / tumble / near settings and for the base density tier. cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_count remains live in every preset and multiplies that base density. The per-feature cvars stay untouched — switching the preset back to 0 returns the user's manual values immediately. _size is intentionally NOT preset-controlled. 0 = manual. 1 = performance. 2 = balanced. 3 = rich (default). Effective only when cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d is on.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_size0.03..3.0 (default 0.2)flake size multiplier. Scales the per-flake half-size at spawn (base 6 world units, plus a small 0.7..1.3 jitter) by this value. 0.03 = microscopic snow dust, 0.2 (default) = fine snow, 3.0 = oversized blizzard flakes. Applies to newly spawned flakes — already-alive flakes keep their original size until they fall out of the pool. Range 0.03..3.0.
cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_tumble0=frozen / 1=tumble (default)per-flake tumble. 1 (default) rotates each flake's axis_v in place around its axis_u with a per-flake angular velocity in the 0.2..1.5 rad/sec range (one revolution every 4..31 seconds), sign 50/50 either direction. Flakes appear to gently spin as they fall — reads as living snowfall rather than a frozen scatter. Pure CPU work (one trig call + Gram-Schmidt re-orthogonalisation per live flake per frame); no GL state involved. 0 = freeze flake orientation at spawn (cheaper; static look). Effective only when cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d is on. When cl_avfx_snow_flakes_3d_quality is non-zero this cvar is overridden by the preset.
cl_avfx_snow_flashlight_detail_preservedefault 0.85 / range 0..1 / step 0.05 / lying snow onlyHow much snow relief / texture detail is kept after the flashlight lift on LYING SNOW (TZ 2026-06-02). Replaces the old flat white-preserve (which mixed toward a single luminance and erased relief) with a chroma-neutralizing blend that keeps local luminance/relief variation. 1 = keep nearly all relief; 0 = old flatter white-preserve behavior. 0.85 (default) keeps snow reading as textured snow inside the cone. Lying snow only; non-snow materials unaffected.
cl_avfx_snow_flashlight_gaindefault 0.45 / range 0..2 / step 0.05Multiplier on the flashlight contribution to snow only — applied before the soft-knee compression. Lower = less brightening of snow inside the flashlight cone (good for already-bright daytime snow). Higher = more brightening (good for dim night snow if you want it to read more under the cone). At 0 the flashlight has no extra effect on snow (snow stays at its celestial-lit base). At 0.45 (default) the cone gives a soft visible lift without blowing out. At 2.0 the snow-local boost is strong; pair with _soft_knee and _white_preserve to keep it from clipping.
cl_avfx_snow_flashlight_headroom_responsedefault 1.00 / range 0..2 / step 0.05 / lying snow onlyExisting-light / luminance headroom gate for LYING SNOW only (TZ 2026-06-02). The brighter the snow already is from moon / sun / celestial / local light, the LESS additional visible light the flashlight adds — so bright moonlit snow no longer turns into a flat white blob. This is not a binary on/off: dim and moderately lit snow still get a proportional flashlight boost; only near-saturated snow strongly suppresses the extra lift. 0 = old accepted behavior (no headroom suppression); 1 (default) = physically-plausible rolloff; 2 = aggressive suppression on bright snow. Ordinary walls / models / water / puddles keep the accepted global flashlight brightness.
cl_avfx_snow_flashlight_luma_ceilingdefault 0.92 / range 0.50..1.20 / step 0.01 / lying snow onlyLocal LDR brightness target the flashlight approaches on LYING SNOW instead of blindly pushing toward pure white (TZ 2026-06-02). Pre-HDR safety ceiling: flashlight-lit snow brightens toward this value, not past it, so relief and texture survive. Lower = the flashlight tops out dimmer and preserves more detail on bright snow; higher = allows brighter snow before suppression kicks in. Lying snow only; non-snow materials unaffected. The future HDR pipeline may replace or reinterpret this.
cl_avfx_snow_flashlight_responsedefault 1.00 / 0=legacy, 1=full snow-specific compression / range 0..1 / step 0.05Master blend for the snow-material-specific flashlight response curve. 0 = legacy behavior (flashlight contribution feeds the same lift-to-vec3(2.0) as lightning / dlight / emissive — under bright flashlight on snow this clips into a flat overbright blob, PO Bugs/60 screenshot 2026-05-28). 1 = full snow-specific compression: the flashlight contribution to snow is gain-scaled, soft-knee compressed against snow albedo luminance, and the lit color is pushed back toward its own luminance to stay snow-white. Other materials (walls, water, puddles, models) are NOT affected — flashlight stays at the accepted global brightness everywhere else. Pair with cl_avfx_snow_flashlight_gain, _soft_knee, _white_preserve.
cl_avfx_snow_flashlight_soft_kneedefault 0.65 / range 0..1 / step 0.05Highlight rolloff strength keyed on snow albedo luminance. At 0 there is no soft-knee — gain is applied flat (legacy-like behavior for already-bright snow). At 1 the gain is fully attenuated by the inverse of snow luminance — already-bright snow gets little additional boost, dark snow gets the full multiplier. 0.65 (default) is a balanced rolloff: dark snow brightens noticeably, near-white snow only gets a gentle nudge so the cone center doesn't clip to a flat blob.
cl_avfx_snow_flashlight_white_preservedefault 0.80 / range 0..1 / step 0.05When the flashlight is the dominant local boost on a snow fragment (out-ranks lightning / amplified dlight / emissive), push the lit color toward its own luminance so the result stays visually white instead of tinting or clipping inside the cone. 0 = no white preservation (lit color is whatever the lift produces). 1 = fully push toward greyscale of the lit luminance. 0.80 (default) keeps snow reading as snow-white in the cone while still allowing slight celestial tint at the edges.
cl_avfx_snow_footprint_fade_rate0.1..20.0 (default 1.0)Snow footprint fade-speed multiplier. Footprints still depend on snowfall / snow fill, but this cvar scales how quickly they are covered back up. 1 = normal, 0.1 = 10x slower / longer-lasting tracks, 10 = 10x faster, 20 = maximum fast fade.
cl_avfx_snow_footprint_strength0..1 (default 0.65)Per-step footprint carve strength. Higher values make each step darker/deeper; lower values leave subtle shallow marks.
cl_avfx_snow_footprints0=off / 1=on (default)Enable local-player footprints in GPU snow. Footsteps carve visible marks into the snow field and refill as snow accumulation continues.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu0=baseline / 1=enable GPU material (default)GPU snow material master toggle. Adds a fragment-shader pass on top of accumulated AVFX snow primitives with world-space noise, cold tint, relief illusion and optional sparkle. The shader runs only where CPU validity authorises snow. Default 1 for snow-enabled AVFX profiles; master AVFX and the snow preset remain opt-in.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_clumpy_edge0=off (default) / 1=onOptional snow clump pattern near snow/bare boundaries. Intended for subtle irregularity at exposed edges; main soft boundary remains controlled by edge feather settings.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_clumpy_freq0.02..2.0 (default 0.18)Frequency/scale of the optional snow clump pattern at boundaries. Lower values make larger, softer clumps; higher values make finer grain.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_continuity0=stop at face boundaries / 1=carry across adjacent floors (default)Additive support layer that carries snow across adjacent static BSP floors so a snow field does not end in a hard break exactly on a BSP face boundary. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_coverage0/1 (default 1)world-XY snow coverage atlas. When ON, the C4 material output is multiplied by a CPU-built atlas tracking snow coverage over time, so the level grows into snow instead of appearing instantly. Default 1 for the accepted snow material baseline.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_coverage_prefill0..1 (default 0.0)Snow coverage atlas prefill floor. 0 starts a level clean and lets snow accumulate over time; 1 starts already fully covered. Intermediate values seed partial coverage.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_coverage_res64..1024 (default 1024, snapped)coverage atlas resolution in pixels per axis. Snapped to {64, 128, 256, 512, 1024}. Default 1024 gives fine transitions while keeping memory around 1 MB.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_coverage_tile_px32 or 64 pixels (default 32)Dirty-tile size, in atlas pixels, used by the accelerated backend when it uploads changed parts of the snow coverage atlas. Smaller tiles give tighter bounding boxes on scattered changes and upload less redundant area; larger tiles mean fewer, bigger uploads. Changing the value forces a full coverage rebuild on the next frame so tile geometry stays consistent. Accelerated backend only (cl_avfx_backend 1); the Classic backend ignores this cvar entirely.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=diagnostic (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: GPU-snow diagnostic overlay/print. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_displace0/1 (default 0, reserved / not active)Reserved (not active in this release) — vertex displacement on AVFX snow primitives only. When implemented, will offset snow stamp vertices along the surface normal up to cl_avfx_snow_volume_h_max for a sense of accumulated depth. BSP world geometry will not be displaced.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_drip_wu0..32 world units (default 10)Height, in world units, of the snow drip band that hangs down a vertical face below a snow-covered floor above it. The band is broken up by per-fragment noise so it reads as irregular fingers fading into nothing rather than a painted stripe; 0 removes it. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_edge_feather0=off / 1=on (default)Shader-side soft fade along exposed snow receiver edges. Helps snow end naturally near lava, moving doors, cliffs and unsupported borders instead of cutting as a hard rectangle.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_edge_feather_min_wu0..64 world units (default 12)Lower bound, in world units, for the snow edge feather band. Small receiver faces would otherwise get a feather so narrow that the edge reads as a hard cut; this floor keeps a visible soft edge on them. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_edge_feather_wu1..256 wu (default 24)Width of the soft snow edge fade band in world units. Larger values make boundary transitions wider and softer.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_edge_flat_nz0..1 normal.z (default 0.95)Flatness cutoff used by cl_avfx_snow_gpu_edge_flat_skip: a face counts as flat when the absolute vertical component of its normal is at least this value. Lower it to treat gentle slopes as flat too, raise it to restrict the exemption to almost perfectly level faces. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_edge_flat_skip0=feather every face / 1=skip the feather on flat faces (default)Treat nearly-flat faces as surfaces rather than edges and skip the edge feather and edge noise on them. This is what keeps flat floors near water clean instead of showing a grainy sand-like band along the shoreline. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_edge_noise_wu0..32 wu (default 10)Noise amplitude added to the snow edge fade distance. Prevents perfectly straight fades and makes snow boundaries look more organic.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_exposure0/1 (default 1)top-down ortho exposure FBO that records the closest occluder above each world XY column. the material pass samples it to discard fragments under overhangs / ceilings. Default 1 for the snow material baseline.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_exposure_res256/512/1024/2048/4096 (default 1024)resolution of the exposure FBO (256/512/1024/2048/4096). Higher = finer exposure mask, more memory + render cost. Default 1024 = 4 MB color tex + 4 MB depth renderbuffer; ample for typical Q2 maps.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_exposure_taps1=sharp/cheap / 4=balanced default / 9=smoother edgeQuality of soft snow-edge sampling. 1 is sharper and cheaper, 4 is the default balanced value, 9 is smoother and a little more expensive. It controls how gently snow fades near cover / sky-boundary transitions.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_footprint_depth0..1 (default 1.0)Visual depth multiplier for GPU snow footprints. Controls how strongly footprints affect the snow material depth/parallax channel.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_footprint_size_wu0..256 wu (default 100)Footprint size in world units for the GPU footprint atlas. Larger values make each step wider; smaller values produce tighter boot marks.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_footprints0/1 (default 0, reserved / not active)Reserved (not active in this release) — GPU-rendered boot-print depressions. Existing 2D overlay footprints continue to work in both Шапки and Покров modes. When implemented, will render boot prints as smooth oval depressions in the snow material instead of textured stickers on top.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_footprints_res128..2048 pixels (default 512)Resolution of the footprint atlas that records where players have walked through the snow. Higher values keep footprint edges crisp on large maps at the cost of texture memory; lower values are cheaper and blur the prints. Requires cl_avfx_snow_footprints 1 in addition to the snow chain. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_fringe0=off, receiver-mesh feather only (default) / 1=draw the legacy fringe stampsLegacy stamp overlay that painted a snow fringe past the polygon edge. The receiver-mesh edge feather replaced it, so it is off by default and is kept for A/B comparison against the current edge treatment. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_fringe_alpha0..1 (default 0.45)Per-overlay opacity of the legacy fringe stamps. It scales the alpha byte written by each stamp and therefore only has a visible effect while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_fringe 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_fringe_width_wu0..256 world units (default 56)Width, in world units, of the legacy fringe stamps. Only has a visible effect while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_fringe 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_glitter0.0..1.0 (default 0.15)Snow sparkle strength in the GPU snow shader. Draws tiny round icy glints with a soft halo at world-fixed positions instead of rectangular white marks. The glints also write to the bloom buffer, so gl_bloom, gl_bloom_strength, gl_bloom_threshold and gl_bloom_sigma control the final glow. Active only at snow GPU quality >= normal. 0 = no sparkles; default 0.15.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_lava_melt_noise0..1 (default 0 = clean band)Break-up noise applied to the melt band where snow meets lava. 0 keeps a clean melt edge; higher values give the band a figured, irregular outline. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_lava_melt_slope_only0=fade on all faces near lava / 1=fade on slopes only (default)Restrict the lava melt fade to sloped faces. With it on, flat floors near lava keep a uniform snow fill and only slopes show the melt gradient, which is the accepted look; with it off every face near lava fades. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_material0/1 (default 1)render snow as a GPU material on real BSP world face polygons (not as overlay-quads above the world). This is the accepted production path for the 1.3 snow profile defaults.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_material_alpha0..1 (default 1.0)output alpha for the material pass (0..1). 1.0 = fully opaque snow (default, matches the overlay opacity). Lower values make snow translucent — brush surface beneath shows through. Combined with cl_avfx_snow_gpu_noise / relief / glitter / quality gives runtime control over the visual.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_material_debug_modedefault 0 / 0=off, >0=mode (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: GPU-snow material diagnostic mode (highlights how receivers/materials are classified). 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_material_edge_fade_wu0..256 (default 100)Width of the soft snow-edge transition in world units (0..256, default 100). Higher values make the border between snowy and bare nearby surfaces fade more gently; 0 keeps the edge hard.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_material_min_fill0..1 (default 1; 0=pure organic accumulation, 0.35=soft playable, 0.70=mostly filled)Floor under the source intensity that the surface graph propagates to spill faces. It is not a global coverage prefill: it only raises the level the spill chain carries, so indoor geometry can be judged without waiting for organic accumulation. The effective value still ramps up over time. 0 gives a pure organic accumulation test, 1 is the accepted target. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_mesh_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=overlay (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: GPU-snow mesh diagnostic overlay. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_noise0.0..1.0 (default 0.45)world-noise amplitude in the GPU snow shader. Drives a 2-octave hash noise sampled in world XY (so the pattern is locked to the map's ground plane, not the camera). 0 = no noise modulation; 1 = strongest variation (about ±8% albedo swing). Default 0.45. Effective only when cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_pom0=flatter/cheaper snow / 1=high-quality snowdrift volume (default)High-quality snowdrift volume shader. When enabled, flat GPU snow gains a stronger depth illusion and reads more like accumulated snow mass. Disable it for the cheaper, flatter relief path.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_pom_alpha0..1 (default 0.95)Snowdrift volume strength (0..1, default 0.95). This is the maximum strength of the depth effect; when cl_avfx_snow_gpu_pom_grow_time is enabled, the actual volume grows up to this value over time.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_pom_depth_wu0..32 world units (default 32)Maximum virtual snowdrift height in world units (0..32, default 32). Higher values make the depth illusion taller at grazing angles; the growth timer treats this as the final target height.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_pom_edge_taper0=harder edge / 1=soft snowdrift edge (default)Fade snowdrift volume at the snow boundary. Keeps the raised snow depth from ending as a hard cliff at the edge of the snow-covered area.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_pom_grow_effective0..1 internal/devInternal runtime multiplier produced by cl_avfx_snow_gpu_pom_grow_time. 0 means snowdrift volume has not grown yet; 1 means the configured snowdrift strength/height is fully reached. Not archived; meant for diagnostics, not manual tuning.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_pom_grow_time0=off/immediate volume (default) / 1..3600 seconds = grow snowdrifts over timeOptional snowdrift growth time in seconds. 0 (default) keeps snowdrift volume immediate. When set to 1..3600, the snow first lays down as a flat blanket; then snowdrift volume grows smoothly toward the configured strength/height over at least this many seconds. Weak snowfall can stretch the time; heavy snowfall never makes it shorter than the configured value.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_pom_steps4..32 (default 29)Snowdrift detail / quality (4..32, default 29). Higher values make the depth illusion smoother and more stable, but cost more shader work. Lower values are faster but can look rougher.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_quality0..2 (default 1)quality tier for the GPU snow shader. 0 = low: relief halved, no glitter (cheapest). 1 = normal (default): full noise + relief + glitter on top of base albedo. 2 = high: same as normal but the shader retains all detail at the highest internal precision. Effective only when cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_receivers0/1 (default 1)build receiver inventory of BSP world faces eligible for snow accumulation (upward-facing normal, not sky/liquid/transparent, sky-cache accepted). Default 1 for the snow material baseline.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_relief0.0..1.0 (default 0.35)relief illusion strength in the GPU snow shader. Where the noise dips low, snow gains a cold blue-shadow tint and a subtle darken; where it peaks, a slight rim-lighten. Sells a soft non-flat surface without real geometry. 0 = flat; 1 = strongest tint (default 0.35). Effective only when cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_relief_intensity0..1 (default 1.0)Master strength of snowdrift relief (0..1, default 1.0). At 0 the snow looks flatter; at 1 the snow surface reacts more strongly at grazing angles, making the blanket read as raised snow mass.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_small_face_area_wu20..65536 (menu step 256, default 4096)Small BSP face area threshold in square world units. Higher values treat more narrow/tiny faces as small snow receivers; default 4096. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1 + cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path active; changing it re-classifies BSP receiver faces on the next rebuild.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_small_face_inradius_wu0..256 world units (default 32)Inradius threshold, in world units, below which a BSP face counts as a small snow receiver. Small faces such as stair treads use the tightened material clamp instead of the normal receiver path. Raise it to treat more narrow geometry as small. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill0=only directly sky-exposed faces / 1=spread onto connected floors (default)Master switch for snow spill: snow that reaches a sky-exposed receiver is allowed to spread onto connected floors that have no sky of their own, so a hall next to an open courtyard is snowed rather than bare. With it off, only directly exposed faces carry snow. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_allow_water0=strict fence around every liquid / 1=allow snow beside water (default)Allow snow on dry floors next to water. Water is not lava, so the strict full-liquid fence is not needed there; the lava melt edge is preserved either way. Set it to 0 to restore the strict fence around every liquid. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_alpha0..1 (default 0.75)Global opacity multiplier applied to spilled snow, so indoor spill can read lighter than the directly exposed snow it comes from. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_chain_passes1..32 passes (default 8)Number of propagation passes the spill solver runs. Each pass advances the front by one graph hop, so deep interiors need several; the solver exits early once nothing changes, so a generous value costs little. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_edge0=no edge seeding / 1=seed spill from exposed edges (default)Seed spill from the exposed edges of receiver faces. This is the mechanism that carries snow through a doorway: the exposed edge acts as the source line the spill field grows from. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_fade_wu0..512 world units (default 96)Width, in world units, of the fade band past the full-strength band. It sets how far spilled snow reaches from its seed before it disappears, and therefore how sharp the outer edge of an indoor snow patch looks. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_full_wu0..256 world units (default 0)Width, in world units, of the band around each seed that receives full-strength spill before the falloff starts. 0 means the falloff begins immediately at the seed, which is what produces a visible gradient instead of a saturated flat fill. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_graph0=distance-bounded spill / 1=graph-bounded spill (default)Bound spill by a surface graph of connected upward world faces instead of by distance alone. Snow then propagates only along floors that are actually reachable from a snowed receiver, so it cannot bleed through a wall into an unrelated room. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_graph_max_wu0..4096 world units (default 256)Maximum graph distance, in world units, that spill may travel from a receiver along the surface graph. It is the reach of indoor snow measured along the floor, not through the air. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_graph_segment_min_overlap0..64 world units (default 6)Minimum length, in world units, that two colinear face edges must overlap before the graph treats them as adjacent. Raising it demands a more substantial shared border and rejects incidental touches. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_graph_segment_tol_wu0..64 world units (default 6)Tolerance, in world units, for deciding that two face edges are colinear when the surface graph is built. It is what connects BSP-fragmented brush boundaries and T-junctions that endpoint matching alone would miss. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_max_drop_wu0..512 world units (default 96)Largest vertical drop, in world units, that spill may cross downward from its receiver. It stops snow from falling down deep shafts onto unrelated floors far below. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_max_edge_samples256..65536 samples (default 10124)Upper bound on how many edge sample points the spill builder may take in one map. It is a safety cap for very large maps: raising it improves coverage on huge levels, lowering it bounds the build cost. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_sameplane_wu0..1024 world units (default 256)Proximity radius, in world units, within which two faces are treated as the same spill plane when the spill target list is built. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_small_step_wu0..64 world units (default 12)Vertical difference, in world units, still treated as the same level when spill crosses a threshold. It lets snow bridge a low door sill without painting the riser face itself. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_step_wu1..128 world units (default 20)Spacing, in world units, between seed points placed along an exposed edge. Smaller steps give a smoother spill front at the cost of more seeds; larger steps are cheaper and coarser. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_support_tail0=hard cutoff at the graph limit / 1=soft tail extension (default)Soft-tail extension for claimed spill faces that are far from any receiver along the graph. It is what removes the bare patches those faces used to show under the old hard cutoff; set it to 0 to compare against that older behaviour. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_support_tail_wu0..8192 world units (default 2048)Reach of the soft-tail extension in world units. It is intentionally longer than the ordinary graph reach, since its whole purpose is to cover faces the chain could not reach. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_unreached_amount0..1 (default 0.65)Base snow level given to those unreachable spill faces. Lower values leave them visibly thinner than properly connected snow; 1 makes them indistinguishable from it. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill_unreached_fill0=leave unreachable faces bare / 1=fill them to the base level (default)Give claimed spill faces that have no graph path to any receiver — thin ledges and bridges cut off by vertical drops — a flat base level of snow so they are not left bare. Part of the spill chain: it only matters while cl_avfx_snow_gpu_spill 1. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_submodel_cut_feather_wu0..64 world units (default 8)Width, in world units, of the inward taper drawn where static world snow meets an excluded moving brush such as a lift or door. It is deliberately narrow so the snow tapers into the gap instead of ending in a hard rectangle. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_thickness_growth1..64 (default 10)How quickly the stored snow depth of a receiver grows while snow keeps falling on it. Larger values reach the thick accepted look sooner after a map starts; smaller values keep a thin dusting for much longer. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_gpu_uzory_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=overlay (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: GPU-snow frost-pattern (uzory) diagnostic overlay. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_avfx_snow_mesh_legacy_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=overlay (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: legacy snow-mesh diagnostic overlay. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_avfx_snow_ordinary_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=diagnostic (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: ordinary (non-GPU) snow diagnostic overlay/print. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
cl_avfx_snow_surface_style0..20 (default 1)TZ 2026-06-22 — snow surface material style. Picks the tile used by the snow material (C4 body, C7B spill/fringe stamps, caps and volume). 0 = Classic (legacy pics/q2prox/avfx/snow_blanket.png); 1..20 = reference-derived natural snow tiles under pics/q2prox/avfx/ss/s1.png..s20.png (fine powder, crystal grain, wind-brushed crust, soft drifts, blue ice, dimpled drift, etc.). Applies live with no vid_restart; a missing tile falls back to Classic. Use the existing noise/relief/glitter/quality controls for strength.
cl_avfx_snow_volume0=flat only / 1=volume on near cells (default)extruded 3D snow volume on near-range Покров cells. When 1 (default), accumulated snow cells within cl_avfx_snow_volume_near_wu of the camera render as raised caps with visible side bevels on exposed edges; mid/far cells beyond that radius keep the cheap flat overlay; cells beyond cl_avfx_render_lod_wu remain culled. Sky-gate inheritance: only cells already accepted by the strict v9.22 sky cache get volume — no indoor leak. 0 = always flat (legacy behavior).
cl_avfx_snow_volume_align_surface0=world-axis cells (default) / 1=align cells to surface texture axesAlign snow volume cells to the texture axes of the floor brush instead of to world axes. On maps whose floor textures are rotated this makes the cell grid follow the visible surface direction; on maps with plain axis-aligned textures the two are identical. Requires cl_avfx 1 + cl_avfx_world 1, the snow preset (cl_avfx_preset 2) and cl_avfx_snow_accum 1 with the GPU receiver path cl_avfx_snow_gpu 1.
cl_avfx_snow_volume_growth0.05..4.0 (default 0.35)snow depth growth rate relative to coverage. Multiplier on AddHit for the depth byte: depth_step = coverage_step × growth. 0.35 (default) means depth fills ~3× slower than coverage so the visible blanket appears quickly while the volume thickens gradually over the session. 1.0 = depth and coverage grow at the same rate. >1.0 = depth saturates first (looks like fresh deep snow on bare ground — uncommon). <0.1 = volume barely lifts even at full coverage.
cl_avfx_snow_volume_h_max0..32 wu (default 10.0)saturation snow depth in world units. Per-cell volume height grows with the cell's depth byte through a smoothstep curve up to this ceiling, modulated by per-cell jitter so neighbour heights vary slightly. Default 10.0 wu is the accepted baseline: visible accumulation without turning surfaces into slabs. 4-6 = light dusting / shallow snow. 8-12 = visible accumulation. 16-32 = blizzard drift / debug. Effective only when cl_avfx_snow_volume is on.
cl_avfx_snow_volume_near_wu0..4096 wu (default 4096)radius in world units within which volume geometry is built. Cells beyond this radius (but still within cl_avfx_render_lod_wu) fall back to the cheap flat overlay; the volume cap stays a near-range visual. Default 4096 wu keeps the accepted snow look stable across q2dm1-scale movement. Lower values reduce volume CPU/GPU cost. Combined with LOD: effective volume range = min(this, cl_avfx_render_lod_wu when LOD on).
cl_avfx_snow_volume_uv_scale16..256 wu (default 184)snow blanket texture tile size in world units. Sets how many world units cover one repetition of the snow grain texture. Default 184 wu/tile is the accepted baseline: calmer large-scale grain with less tiled noise. Texture is sampled at world-projected UVs so adjacent cells share a continuous grain stream. Asset is pics/q2prox/avfx/snow_blanket.png; falls back to the round-alpha particle texture if missing.
cl_avfx_snow_wall_smear0=off (default) / 1=onTZ 2026-07-02 — optional vertical wall snow smear. When on, a light snow film clings a limited distance up STATIC BSP walls that share a real edge with an adjacent snow-covered floor receiver. Additive and isolated: never changes the accepted floor/spill/continuity snow, never runs on movers (doors/plats/lifts), sky/warp/liquid/nodraw faces, ceilings/undersides, or no-contact lethal voids. The film is bottom-up + organic-topped, seeded from the neighbouring floor's visible snow, and honours Distance LOD. Weapon impacts on a smeared wall leave snow marks using the real wall normal. Off by default; tune height/opacity/noise in the Edges submenu.
cl_avfx_snow_wall_smear_alpha0..1 (default 0.35)TZ 2026-07-02 — opacity of the wall snow smear. 0 = invisible, 1 = full snow opacity. Combined with the floor's own visible snow amount and the global snow-material alpha, so the restrained default reads as a subtle wind-blown residue, not an opaque sheet.
cl_avfx_snow_wall_smear_clump_scale0.3..3.0 (default 1.0)TZ 2026-07-02 — wall snow clump size. Higher values make the clumps smaller and more frequent (finer granular snow); lower values make fewer, larger clumps. Live tuning knob for the wall-snow look.
cl_avfx_snow_wall_smear_density0..1 (default 0.5)TZ 2026-07-02 — wall snow coverage amount. Shifts the clump acceptance threshold: higher = the clumps cover more of the wall (denser), lower = sparser scattered clumps. Live tuning knob.
cl_avfx_snow_wall_smear_fill_ratio1..20 (default 5)TZ 2026-07-02 — how many times SLOWER the wall snow fills in than the horizontal floor it grows from. 1 = same speed as the floor; 5 (default) = wall builds up 5x slower; 20 = very gradual. The wall opacity ramps over time and never outruns the floor's own fill, so wall snow lags behind floor snow naturally.
cl_avfx_snow_wall_smear_height_wu8..512 wu (default 48)TZ 2026-07-02 — how far the wall snow smear climbs up the wall, in world units. Kept low by default so it reads as a thin residue hugging the floor/step contact; the reach varies along the wall and the top breaks up organically (see the noise toggle). On stairs each step gets its own thin band. Only meaningful with cl_avfx_snow_wall_smear 1.
cl_avfx_snow_wall_smear_noise0=smooth / 1=organic (default)TZ 2026-07-02 — organic top edge for the wall snow smear. 1 = the upper boundary is eroded by world-locked noise so it reads as packed snow dust / wind residue rather than a straight painted line. 0 = a plain smooth gradient top.
cl_avfx_snow_water_effects0=off / 1=snow water contacts (default)Snow-on-water contact effects for the snow preset. When a falling snow sample reaches sky-exposed CONTENTS_WATER, Q2PRO-X keeps the water as water and adds a soft low-strength ripple plus small pale drifting melt specks on the surface; a small fraction of specks also emits bloom-capable icy glints. Lava/slime are excluded and keep their own steam path. Independent of cl_avfx_water: the contact layer can render even if the enhanced water shader is off. Subject to cl_avfx_world and the open-sky gate.
cl_avfx_snow_water_patch_density0..1 (default 0.45)Visible density/chance for drifting snow melt patches on water, 0..1.
