cl_demo_analytics_trail_outline_color#rrggbb or named color, default #000000Colour of the outline particle drawn behind trail dots and HUD event dots (requires trail_outline 1). Accepts #rrggbb and named colours via SCR_ParseColor. Default is solid black #000000.
cl_demo_analytics_trail_outline_scalefloat >= 1, default 1.6Size multiplier of the outline particle relative to the foreground dot. 1.6 means the outline is 60 % wider on each side. Must be >= 1.
cl_demo_analytics_trail_stride1 .. 20, default 1Per-slot sample thinning in trail mode. 1 = draw every live sample (densest trail). N = draw every Nth live sample per player slot — dots become more spaced apart, and line segments (when trail_lines is on) become longer. This is a draw-time filter only; the underlying cached dataset is untouched, so no rescan is needed. Clamped to [1, 20].
cl_demo_analytics_window_sec5 .. 600 seconds, default 60Sliding-window size in seconds for time_scope = window. Ignored when time_scope is full or elapsed.
cl_demo_analytics_world_adaptive_colors0=off (default) / 1=onAnalytics adaptive colours — when on, the toggle expands cl_vis_*_color highlight palette across multiple analytics surfaces: - recognized item pickup dots in world rendering AND HUD overview both pull from the item-class highlight palette (overrides cl_demo_analytics_pickup_color only for those dots) - in trail mode, player-traffic dots AND connecting lines pull from per-player highlight colours via the player visibility palette (cl_vis_players_* mode dispatch — team / duel / FFA / model / all / off→FFA-fallback). Off-mode falls through to FFA palette so each slot still gets a distinct stable colour Aggregate-mode heatmap traffic cells, frag dots, and trail outlines are NOT adaptive — they keep their manual cvars. Unsupported / ambiguous pickups fall back to cl_demo_analytics_pickup_color. Demo-only — no effect outside playback. Off by default. LOCAL scope (demo_visual cfg). Cvar name kept for backwards compatibility — its actual scope spans world + HUD + trail.
cl_demo_analytics_world_alpha0.0 .. 1.0, default 0.35Alpha of in-world particles (used when cl_demo_analytics_style is world or both). Applied to traffic heatmap cells, frag dots, and pickup dots in 3D space.
cl_demo_analytics_world_lifetime_sec0.0 .. 60.0 seconds, default 0.0 (aggregate)Trail mode for in-world particles. 0 (default) = aggregate: every collected sample/event is drawn at once at flat alpha (traffic uses binned heat cells). >0 = trail: each sample/event becomes its own dot that appears at the moment it was recorded (sample.t == cl.servertime) and fades linearly to fully transparent over this many seconds. In trail mode traffic is drawn per-sample (not via binned cells) so you see actual movement trails growing behind players as the demo plays. Does not affect the HUD panel — the HUD still follows cl_demo_analytics_time_scope.
cl_demo_analytics_world_scale0.25 .. 4.0, default 1.0Size multiplier for in-world particles. 1.0 = default (traffic ~8 units, pickup ~6 units, frag ~10 units). Independent from cell_size; this only affects visible particle scale in 3D.
cl_demo_browser_alpha0.0 .. 1.0, default 0.85Demo browser overlay background opacity, [0.0, 1.0]. Independent from scr_alpha. Applied on top of SCR_OledGetUiAlpha() when OLED UI-protection is enabled, so the overlay dims in sync with the rest of the Q2PRO-X UI during the OLED breathe.
cl_demo_browser_fullscreen0=windowed (default) / 1=fullscreenMaximize the demo browser overlay to fill the entire HUD. When on, the window spans the full screen and the resize grip + title-bar drag are suppressed (the previous geometry cvars are preserved and restored when fullscreen is toggled back off). Also toggled by the [F] button in the overlay header, same contract as the server browser.
cl_demo_browser_hHUD pixels, 0 = autoDemo browser overlay height in HUD pixels. 0 = recompute from HUD extents each open (82% tall). See cl_demo_browser_w.
cl_demo_browser_last_taball / favorites / date / mod / map / pov (default "all")Internal archived cvar that holds the last opened demo browser tab as a stable string name ("all", "favorites", "date", "mod", "map", "pov"). Read on browser open when cl_demo_browser_remember_tab is on, written on every tab switch. Legacy integer values from older configs are accepted and rewritten in string form on the next switch.
cl_demo_browser_pillarbox_workspace0=content rect / 1=full window (default)When pillarbox (letterbox) display is active, draw the demo browser overlay into the full window rather than the narrower game content rect. Matches the analogous behaviour in the server browser.
cl_demo_browser_remember_tab0=always start on All / 1=restore last tab (default)Restore the last opened demo browser tab (All / Favorites / Date / Mod / Map / POV) on next session. When off, the browser always starts on All. The current tab is recorded in cl_demo_browser_last_tab whenever you switch tabs.
cl_demo_browser_row_colors0=uniform rows / 1=alternate row colors (default)Alternate row background colour in the demo browser list for readability (zebra-stripe style). Selection highlight is drawn on top regardless.
cl_demo_browser_scale0.1 .. 3.0, default 1.5Demo browser overlay text and chrome scale, [0.1, 3.0]. Independent from scr_scale. Same scaling model as the cvar browser: the atlas stays fixed and the overlay picks its on-screen glyph size from this multiplier. 0.1 packs the maximum number of rows into the list, 1.0 is the baseline, 3.0 is the largest readable preset.
cl_demo_browser_show_broken0=hide partial+unreadable / 1=show partial+unreadable (default)Single toggle that governs visibility of non-OK rows. Covers BOTH partial (playable but metadata parse was incomplete — amber tint) AND unreadable (file couldn't be opened or the stream had no readable first message — red tint). Partial rows stay selectable and playable; the missing metadata may even fill in automatically once playback starts. Query term broken:1 / broken:0 still works for explicit filtering.
cl_demo_browser_show_details0=hide detail pane / 1=show detail pane (default)Enable the right-side detail pane in the demo browser. When off, the list pane spans the full window width and the detail pane is hidden; selected-demo metadata is still reachable via the status bar and keyboard actions.
cl_demo_browser_show_packed0=hide packed entries (default) / 1=show demos from engine packsInclude demos discovered inside engine-visible pack / container sources (pak / pkx / etc.) in the browser listing. Off by default so the browser feels like the user's personal demo library rather than "everything the engine FS can see". Engine precedence is preserved — a demo that exists both on disk and in a pack shows as the on-disk entry without a packed marker.
cl_demo_browser_wHUD pixels, 0 = autoDemo browser overlay width in HUD pixels. 0 = recompute from HUD extents each open (88% wide). Updated live during resize-grip drag and clamped to the minimum usable width.
cl_demo_browser_xHUD pixels, sentinel = centredDemo browser overlay top-left X position in HUD space. Defaults to centred on first open. Updated live via header drag and on window resize; saved back to the cvar so geometry survives restart. Value INT_MIN is the sentinel for 'use centred default'.
cl_demo_browser_yHUD pixels, sentinel = centredDemo browser overlay top-left Y position in HUD space. See cl_demo_browser_x.
cl_demo_index_autoscan0=manual browser refresh / 1=refresh on each browser open (default)Refresh the shared demo index incrementally in the background whenever the Demo Browser opens. Cached records stay visible immediately. Off disables this automatic request; manual refresh and automatic game statistics remain independent.
cl_demomsglen0..3Specifies default maximum message size used for demo recording. Default value is 1390. See record command description for more information on demo packet sizes.
cl_demoplayer_gun0=show gun (default) / 1=hide gunGun model while watching a demo or an MVD stream from the recorded player's eyes. Overrides only playback; live play keeps cl_gun.
cl_demoplayer_hide_draws0=always draw items / 1=hide items during demo playback (default)Suppress user-supplied draw command items (e.g. draw cl_timer, draw cl_lag, draw cl_ping) while a demo is playing. When on (default), the entire draw-object list is skipped during demo playback so HUD text from live-game sessions doesn't overlay onto demo viewing. Live-game HUD is never affected. Applies to both .dm2 and .mvd2 playback.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_autoplaydefault 0 / 0 or 1Demo-player online music autoplay. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_autoplay_resultsdefault 0 / 0 or 1Demo-player auto-play results. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_base_urldefault https://promodj.com/musicDemo-player online music base URL. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_enabledefault 0 / 0 or 1Demo-player online music master. Separate global profile (off by default).
cl_demoplayer_music_online_end_modedefault 0 / 0/1/2Demo-player end mode: 0 stop, 1 repeat all, 2 repeat one. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_genre_modedefault 0 / 0/1/2Demo-player genre mode: 0 all, 1 selected, 2 random. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_lucky_continuousdefault 1 / 0 or 1Demo-player lucky continuous. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_lucky_scopedefault 0 / 0/1/2Demo-player lucky scope: 0 selected, 1 random genre, 2 all. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_pause_with_demodefault 0 / 0 or 1Pause demo-player online music together with the demo. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_preferred_genresdefault emptyDemo-player preferred genres (';'-separated slugs). Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_providerdefault promodjDemo-player online music provider id. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_queue_modedefault 0 / 0/1Demo-player queue mode: 0 sequential, 1 roulette. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_randomdefault 0 / 0 or 1Demo-player random order. Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_music_online_volumedefault 0.70 / 0.0..1.0Demo-player online music volume (s_volume stays master). Global demo profile.
cl_demoplayer_mvd_directorsee cl_demoplayer_mvd_director_modeLegacy alias. See cl_demoplayer_mvd_director_mode.
cl_demoplayer_mvd_director_lead_sec0.5 .. 10.0 seconds, default 3.0Lead time in seconds used by the next frag Director mode. The Director switches POV to the upcoming fragger this many seconds before the frag happens on the wire, so the user sees the kill from the killer's perspective rather than arriving late. Also used to size the post-manual-override cooldown: after the user hand-picks a POV the Director pauses for max(lead_sec * 3, 3 sec) so the user's pick sticks briefly before auto-switching resumes.
cl_demoplayer_mvd_director_mode0=off (default) / 1=next frag / 2=quad / 3=penta / 4=leaderMVD-only follow mode for the demo-player Director. off leaves POV under manual control. Three current-state modes follow live MVD state: quad and penta chase whoever currently holds the power-up; leader chases the current STAT_FRAGS leader. The exact future-event mode next frag uses the pre-scanned obituary timeline built at demo start (see MVD_PreScanFrags) — POV switches cl_demoplayer_mvd_director_lead_sec seconds BEFORE each frag happens on the wire. The pre-scan is seek/replay resilient and works on the first play; no watch through once step. When the scan finds zero events the Director popover shows next frag (unavailable) and leaves POV alone.
cl_demoplayer_nextfrag_debug0=off (default) / 1=tick / 2=scan (diagnostic, current session only)Diagnostic log for the next frag Director backend. Off by default. tick prints the Director's per-tick decision (current demo time, next event, gap, lead, fire=YES/no) and dumps the full frag timeline at scan completion. scan adds per-obituary accept/reject logs from the pre-scan (which lines the parser treated as kills and why). Use this only when diagnosing a mismatch between the scan timeline and real playback — the tick log is ~2 Hz so it fills the console fast.
cl_demoplayer_noskins0=original skins (default) / 1=no skins (male/grunt)Player skins while watching a demo: as recorded, or everyone drawn as male/grunt. Overrides only playback; live play keeps cl_noskins.
cl_demoplayer_overlay0=off / 1=on (default)Master switch for the modern demo player overlay. When on (default), a playback control bar renders at the bottom of the HUD during every demo and the legacy scr_demobar is automatically suppressed so the two progress indicators never stack. When off, this overlay produces no output at all and the engine falls back to whatever scr_demobar is configured to do.
cl_demoplayer_overlay_alpha0.0 .. 1.0, default 0.9Background opacity of the demo player overlay, [0.0, 1.0]. Independent from scr_alpha. Applied on top of SCR_OledGetUiAlpha() when OLED UI-protection is enabled.
cl_demoplayer_overlay_autohide_sec0 .. 60 seconds, default 5Auto-hide threshold for the demo player. After this many seconds without a real key-down event the player hides entirely. Mouse motion is intentionally NOT an activity signal — raw-input sensor noise and warp echoes during grabbed playback would otherwise starve the timer. Once hidden, the player stays hidden: incidental keystrokes neither wake it nor are interpreted by the player — they go to the game as usual. It returns only via explicit reopen paths: the bound demo_player_toggle key or the menu's open interactive player... action. 0 keeps the player pinned while a demo plays.
cl_demoplayer_overlay_scale0.5 .. 3.0, default 1.2Text and chrome scale for the demo player overlay, [0.5, 3.0]. Independent from scr_scale. Scales the button glyphs, timeline thickness, and padding by the same multiplier.
cl_demoplayer_overlay_seek_jump_sec1 .. 600 seconds, default 50Seconds that the [<<] and [>>] jump-seek buttons jump by. Used for coarse scrubbing when timeline-dragging isn't precise enough. User-tuned value is saved in the global Q2PRO-X config.
cl_demoplayer_overlay_seek_step_sec1 .. 120 seconds, default 10Seconds that the [<] and [>] step-seek buttons jump by. Used on both single-click in interactive mode and on the keyboard Left/Right arrow shortcut. User-tuned value is saved in the global Q2PRO-X config.
cl_demoplayer_overlay_show_score0=hide [score] button / 1=show (default)Show the MVD-only [score] button in the interactive transport row when playing an .mvd2 demo. The button runs the score command, which pops up the scoreboard if the mod supports it. Ignored for .dm2 playback.
cl_demoplayer_overlay_yHUD pixels from bottom, default 0Vertical offset of the overlay from the bottom of the HUD, in HUD pixels. 0 = flush to the bottom. Raise this if a mod HUD element (kill feed, net graph, etc.) covers the default position. Capped at half the HUD height to keep the overlay visible.
cl_demoplayer_volume0.0 .. 1.0, default 0.7Demo-playback sound multiplier applied on top of the live s_volume master. Final demo gain is s_volume * cl_demoplayer_volume (and then runtime mute/fade if active). Implemented as an in-memory mixer multiplier — s_volume is NEVER rewritten, so a crash / alt+F4 / forced disconnect mid-demo cannot leak this value into the user's saved config. When a demo starts the overlay calls S_SetVolumeOverride(this_value); when the demo ends it clears the multiplier. Slider is also reachable via the vol N popover pill in the demo-player bar.
cl_demosnaps0..300Specifies time interval, in seconds, between saving snapshots in memory during demo playback. Snapshots enable backward seeking in demo (see seek command description), and speed up repeated forward seeks. Setting this variable to 0 disables snapshotting entirely. Default value is 10.
cl_demosuspendtoggle0/1Specifies if suspend both pauses and resumes demo recording or just pauses if it was recoring. Default value is 1 (toggle between pause and resume).
cl_demowait0/1Specifies if demo playback is automatically paused at the last frame in demo file. Default value is 0 (finish playback).
cl_game_stats_alpha0.0 .. 1.0, default 0.85Game Statistics overlay background opacity, [0.0, 1.0]. Independent from scr_alpha. Applied on top of SCR_OledGetUiAlpha() so the overlay dims in sync with the rest of the Q2PRO-X UI during the OLED breathe.
cl_game_stats_auto0=off (default) / 1=refresh on an eligible cold startRefresh the Demo Library automatically on an eligible cold idle start. Off by default, and off means genuinely zero background work: no directory walk, no demo parsing, no worker job and no intro cards. A direct +map, connect, demo or URL start is never eligible, so a launch that goes straight into a game never triggers analysis.
cl_game_stats_days0 .. 3650 days, default 7Statistics period, in whole LOCAL CALENDAR days. 0 means today since local midnight; 7 means from local midnight seven calendar days ago, inclusive. The cutoff is converted through the OS timezone and DST rules, so a 23- or 25-hour day is handled correctly; it is never now minus N*86400 and never a date taken from the file name. Widening the window analyses only demos whose match facts are missing. Narrowing it analyses nothing at all.
cl_game_stats_debug0=off (default) / 1=summary / 2=verbose; session-only, never archived (diagnostic, current session only)Diagnostic verbosity for the Demo Library and the statistics query. Session-only by project policy: it is accepted from the command line or console for this process, is never loaded from or written to any config, and costs nothing while it is 0.
cl_game_stats_detail_wretired — always 0; see cl_game_stats_layoutRetired. The detail pane width used to be stored here in HUD pixels, which meant a layout saved at one resolution was wrong at every other. It now lives as a proportion inside cl_game_stats_layout. An existing value is converted once on the first draw, after which this is set to 0 and never read again. Nothing sets it any more; leave it alone.
cl_game_stats_fullscreen0=off (default) / 1=fullscreenMaximize the statistics overlay to fill the whole HUD; the resize grip is hidden while this is on and the stored window geometry is left untouched.
cl_game_stats_h0 = automatic; otherwise HUD pixelsGame Statistics overlay height in HUD pixels. 0 means pick a sensible default from the current HUD size. Updated automatically when you drag the resize grip.
cl_game_stats_intro0=off / 1=on (default)While the startup intro plays, show a short sequence of personal moments beside the main menu: ONE fact at a time, flying in, holding a single readable instant, then widening and dissolving. There is no panel, no frame and no card — typography and its own light are the whole scene, and an echo never covers the logo, the menu, the controls or the status line. On by default, but inert unless BOTH automatic statistics and the intro itself are active. Only unambiguous real matches of the current player with a proven positive contribution are counted here — never the overall session count, never another player's data. With no qualifying match, nothing is drawn at all rather than a zero-filled scene.
cl_game_stats_intro_combat0=hide / 1=show (default)Include personal frags and deaths in the startup Intro.
cl_game_stats_intro_death_weapon0=hide / 1=show (default)Include the weapon that killed the current player most often in the startup Intro.
cl_game_stats_intro_greeting0=hide / 1=show (default)Include the player greeting and analysed calendar span in the startup Intro statistics sequence.
cl_game_stats_intro_items0=hide all item lines / 1=show every item line (default)Include every strategic pickup found in accepted matches as its own cinematic line on every startup Intro. Items are never rotated between launches.
cl_game_stats_intro_kill_weapon0=hide / 1=show (default)Include the weapon used for the most kills in the startup Intro.
cl_game_stats_intro_last_game0=hide / 1=show (default)Include the newest counted demo date in the startup Intro statistics sequence.
cl_game_stats_intro_map0=hide / 1=show (default)Include the most-played map in the startup Intro.
cl_game_stats_intro_matches0=hide / 1=show (default)Include the meaningful personal match count in the startup Intro.
cl_game_stats_intro_mod0=hide / 1=show (default)Include the favorite game mod in the startup Intro.
cl_game_stats_intro_opponent0=hide / 1=show (default)Include the most frequent opponent in the startup Intro.
cl_game_stats_intro_results0=hide / 1=show (default)Include wins, losses and draws in the startup Intro.
cl_game_stats_last_tabsummary / matches / opponents / maps / modes / dataInternal: the stable identifier of the statistics tab that was open last. Written by the overlay, read back when cl_game_stats_remember_tab is on.
cl_game_stats_layoutwritten by the overlay; game_stats_layout_reset restores defaultsThe single versioned record of everything you arranged by hand in the Game Statistics overlay: column proportions, whether the detail pane is open and how wide, sort column and direction, and which mode sections are collapsed. Everything is stored as a PROPORTION, so a layout arranged at 3840x2160 still looks right at 1280x720. Search text, the selected row, scroll position and focus are deliberately NOT saved: reopening the overlay mid-search would be a bug, not a convenience. A string that does not parse is not partially applied — the overlay starts from defaults and says so once. game_stats_layout_reset clears it.
cl_game_stats_min_size_kb1 .. no maximum, in KiB, default 40Smallest demo, in kibibytes, that Game Statistics will look at. A few kilobytes of demo is a connect and a disconnect, not a match, and counting those distorts every rate on the Summary tab. This is a filter over facts already in memory: changing it re-answers instantly and reparses nothing, and the Demo Browser still lists every file regardless. Excluded files are counted on the Data tab rather than silently dropped. The floor is 1 KiB; there is no ceiling, because how large a real match has to be is your judgement.
cl_game_stats_namesempty = just the current name; otherwise up to 32 comma-separated aliases, always plus the current nameComma-separated list of your OTHER nicknames, counted as the same person. The current name is ALWAYS tracked as well — this list extends your identity, it does not replace it, so typing one old nickname can never stop counting the matches you are playing right now. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed, empty entries dropped, duplicates folded, and comparison ignores letter case and the high-bit form server names use. The picker beside the field offers only names your own recordings were actually made under. Changing this list is a query over facts already in memory: no demo is ever re-read because you renamed yourself.
cl_game_stats_pillarbox_workspace0=off / 1=on (default)Use the full presentation surface, including the pillarbox bars, as the statistics overlay workspace, so the window can be dragged into the black side areas on a non-matching aspect ratio.
cl_game_stats_remember_tab0=off / 1=on (default)Reopen the statistics overlay on whichever tab (Summary / Matches / Opponents / Maps / Modes / Data) was active last time. Off means always start on Summary. The internal cl_game_stats_last_tab stores the name.
cl_game_stats_row_colors0=off / 1=on (default)Alternate the row background colour in the statistics lists for readability.
cl_game_stats_scale0.1 .. 3.0, default 1.5Game Statistics overlay text and chrome scale, [0.1, 3.0]. Independent from scr_scale; the atlas stays fixed and the overlay picks its on-screen glyph size from this multiplier.
cl_game_stats_show_details0=off / 1=on (default)Show the detail pane beside the table. It describes the selected row instead of repeating it: where a result came from, the recorded final table, the mode-correct relation to an opponent, and a list of recent matches you can open or play. Hidden on Summary and Data, which are totals with no selected row to describe. Its width and open state are remembered per tab in cl_game_stats_layout.
cl_game_stats_w0 = automatic; otherwise HUD pixelsGame Statistics overlay width in HUD pixels. 0 means pick a sensible default from the current HUD size. Updated automatically when you drag the resize grip.
cl_game_stats_x-2147483648 = auto-centre; otherwise HUD pixelsGame Statistics overlay window X position in HUD pixels. The sentinel -2147483648 means auto-centre. Updated automatically when you drag the overlay by its title bar.
cl_game_stats_y-2147483648 = auto-centre; otherwise HUD pixelsGame Statistics overlay window Y position in HUD pixels. The sentinel -2147483648 means auto-centre. Updated automatically when you drag the overlay by its title bar.

Graphics, shaders and cache

Variables in this section: 229.

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
gl_allow_software0=reject software OpenGL / 1=allow software OpenGLAllow Windows/WGL to fall back to a software OpenGL implementation if no hardware accelerated context is available. Normally leave 0 — software OpenGL is far too slow for Quake 2. Startup/vid_restart diagnostic only.
gl_angle_backendauto/d3d11/vulkanANGLE backend used by the win32egl video driver. auto uses the stable D3D11 path; Vulkan is an explicit experimental mode for future GLES 3.1/3.2 renderer work. Startup/vid_restart cvar.
gl_anisotropy1..16When set to 2 and higher, enables anisotropic filtering of world textures, if supported by your OpenGL implementation. Default value is 1 (anisotropic filtering disabled).
gl_beamstyle0=textured billboard beam / 1=flat polygonal beamSpecifies drawing style of laser beams. Default value is 0.
gl_bilerp_chars0/1Enables bilinear filtering of charset images. Default value is 0 (disabled).
gl_bilerp_pics0=disabled for all pictures / 1=enabled for large pictures that dont fit into the scrap / 2=enabled for all pictures, including the scrap texture itselfEnables bilinear filtering of HUD pictures. Default value is 1.
gl_bilerp_skies0/1Enables bilinear filtering of skybox textures. Default value is 1 (enabled).
gl_bloom0=off / 1..8=bloom enabled, blur quality/iterationsEnable re-release bloom effect. Only effective when using GLSL backend. Default value is 0 (disabled). Higher values specify number of blurring filter iterations (typical value is 1). Code clamps to 1..8 when enabled.
gl_bloom_ammo_percent0..100; default 100Ammunition: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_armor_percent0..100; default 100Armour: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_blackhole_percent0..100; default 100Black holes: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_glints_percent0..100; default 100Other AVFX glints: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_health_percent0..100; default 100Health: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_keys_percent0..100; default 100Keys: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_lava_percent0..100; default 100Lava: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_lightning_percent0..100; default 100Lightning: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_meteors_percent0..100; default 100Meteors / impacts: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_models_percent0..100; default 100Other models: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_player_weapon_percent0..100; default 100Held weapons: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_players_percent0..100; default 100Players: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_powerup_shell_percent0..100; default 100Active powerup shells: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_powerups_percent0..100; default 100Powerups: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_sigma0.1..10Specifies strength parameter of gaussian blur filter used for the bloom effect. Default value is 4. (or glowmaps disabled) is a waste of resources.
gl_bloom_slime_percent0..100; default 100Slime / acid: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_snow_percent0..100; default 100Snow sparkles: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_stars_percent0..100; default 100Stars / bright planets: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_strength0..5bloom strength multiplier
gl_bloom_sun_percent0..100; default 100Sun: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_threshold0..1bloom brightness threshold
gl_bloom_water_percent0..100; default 100Water: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_weapon_fx_percent0..100; default 100Weapon effects: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_weapons_percent0..100; default 100Map weapons: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_world_emissive_percent0..100; default 100Emissive map textures: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_bloom_world_percent0..100; default 100Other bright surfaces: percentage of common bloom strength; zero skips source bloom calculations without hiding the object.
gl_brightness-1..1Specifies a brightness value that is added to each pixel of world lightmaps. Positive values make lightmaps brighter, negative values make lightmaps darker. Default value is 0 (keep original brightness).
gl_bsp_tess_architecture0=original architecture / 1=tessellated architecture (default)Child master for tessellated relief on solid BSP level architecture: floors, slopes and walls. Turning it off routes those faces through the exact original CPU BSP geometry without changing the saved relief parameters. Geometric water and lava remain independently controlled. Requires the general gl_bsp_tessellation master.
gl_bsp_tess_architecture_floors0=off / 1=on (default)Apply generic BSP architecture relief to floors and upward slopes. Independent from the wall lane and from Brick geometry. Requires both tessellation and architecture masters.
gl_bsp_tess_architecture_walls0=off / 1=on (default)Apply generic BSP architecture relief to walls and ceilings. Independent from the floor lane and from Brick geometry. Requires both tessellation and architecture masters.
gl_bsp_tess_debugdefault 0 / 0=off, >0=overlay (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: WGL BSP hardware-tessellation debug visualization. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
gl_bsp_tess_detail_scale8..256 world units (default 64)World-space scale of the procedural solid-surface relief. Lower values create smaller bumps; higher values create broad hills and uneven walls. Three deterministic noise octaves are evaluated from world position, so the shape never follows the camera.
gl_bsp_tess_edge_guard0.5..32 world units (default 4)World-space width of the fixed guard along every original BSP face perimeter. Displacement fades to exactly zero at the contour, preserving BSP/PVS visibility and preventing cracks or wall-through sight lines.
gl_bsp_tess_force_fallback0=off (default) / 1=force fallback (diagnostic, current session only)Developer diagnostic: never compile the BSP tessellation shaders and draw the non-tessellated fallback, as on hardware without tessellation.
gl_bsp_tess_lava0=off / 1=on (default; requires gl_bsp_tessellation 1)Independent WGL child master for geometric BSP lava waves. It reuses the fixed micro-triangle and sealed-shore path proven by water without changing water, slime, reflections or contact effects.
gl_bsp_tess_lava_height0..16 world units (default 3)Maximum outward lava-wave height. Displacement fades smoothly to zero at the original union-aware shore.
gl_bsp_tess_lava_scale16..512 world units (default 128)Average world-space wavelength for geometric lava. Four deterministic moving bands avoid a repeating geometric pattern.
gl_bsp_tess_lava_speed0..4 (default 0.55)Animation speed multiplier for geometric lava waves. 0 freezes the current shape without disabling the lava geometry.
gl_bsp_tess_lod0=off / 1=on (default)Distance LOD for BSP tessellation. Reduces edge factors toward 1 at long range. Factors are calculated from canonical shared-edge endpoints, so adjacent triangles agree and do not open cracks.
gl_bsp_tess_lod_distance512..8192 (default 2048)Distance in world units where BSP tessellation LOD reaches its minimum factor. The transition begins at 55% of this distance and is smooth.
gl_bsp_tess_quality0=Performance / 1=Balanced / 2=High (default) / 3=UltraBSP tessellation density preset. Performance/Balanced/High/Ultra target approximately 96/64/32/16 world-unit generated edges with bounded hardware factors. Higher values increase GPU geometry work.
gl_bsp_tess_radius0..32 world units (default 12)Maximum outward relief height in world units. Solid BSP detail is non-negative along the effective face normal, so it never retreats behind the original BSP plane and cannot expose hidden geometry. Every original face perimeter converges to zero displacement.
gl_bsp_tess_smoothing0..100 percent (default 60)Strength of camera-invariant procedural relief generated inside solid BSP faces by WGL hardware tessellation. 0 keeps the original plane; 100 applies the full gl_bsp_tess_radius height. The former silhouette-moving Phong deformation is not used. Render-only: collision and server BSP remain unchanged.
gl_bsp_tess_water0=off / 1=on (default; requires gl_bsp_tessellation 1)Geometric tessellated waves for BSP water on the WGL patch path. Supports both transparent and opaque water while preserving the existing material, AVFX, reflection and vertex-colour paths. Lava, slime, portals and sky materials are excluded.
gl_bsp_tess_water_height0..16 world units (default 4)Maximum geometric wave height. Four moving directional bands are combined and their displacement fades to zero at the original shoreline.
gl_bsp_tess_water_scale16..512 world units (default 96)Average world-space wavelength for geometric water. The additional bands use different frequencies and directions to avoid a single repeating wave train.
gl_bsp_tess_water_speed0..4 (default 1)Animation speed multiplier for geometric water waves. 0 freezes the current wave shape without disabling tessellation.
gl_bsp_tessellation0=off (default) / 1=onGeneral hardware tessellation master for eligible static BSP world surfaces. Off by default. It is a renderer feature, not a cheat or a Single Player mutator: multiplayer and Single Player use the same WGL path. Capable desktop OpenGL/WGL uses patches; win32egl and unsupported WGL automatically keep the normal CPU world path without changing the requested value.
gl_celshading0=off / 0.1..10=line thicknessEnables drawing black contour lines around 3D models (aka celshading). Value of this variable specifies thickness of the lines drawn. Default value is 0 (celshading disabled). Code clamps to 0..10.
gl_clear0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)diagnostic: clear the framebuffer each frame to expose unfilled regions
gl_clearcolor#RRGGBB (diagnostic, current session only)diagnostic clear colour used when gl_clear is on
gl_colorbits0=auto / 16 / 24=RGB8 / 30=RGB10A2 / 32Requested total RGB color-buffer depth, excluding alpha. On win32wgl: 0 = match the target monitor (RGB10A2 at 10+ bpc, otherwise RGB8), 24 = RGB8, 30 = exact RGB10A2 attempt; true HDR uses the separate FP16 path. Startup/vid_restart cvar.
gl_coloredlightmaps0/1Enables grayscaling of world lightmaps. 1 keeps original colors, 0 converts lightmaps to grayscale format, any value in between reduces colorfulness. Default value is 1 (keep original colors).
gl_cubemaps0/1Enables use of cubemaps for skybox drawing. Cubemaps allow multiple skybox textures per map, and help to avoid sky rendering bugs. Also enables N64 skies in re-release maps. Only effective if gl_shaders is enabled. Default value is 0 (disabled).
gl_cull_models0/1frustum-cull models
gl_cull_nodes0/1frustum-cull BSP nodes
gl_damageblend_frac0..1damage screen blend intensity
gl_debug0=off / 1=debug context / 2=debug context + stricter diagnostics (diagnostic, current session only)Enable OpenGL debug context for backend diagnostics. Drivers vary in what they report; values above 1 may engage stricter diagnostics where supported. Startup/vid_restart cvar.
gl_debug_distfrac0..1 (diagnostic, current session only)debug dist-fraction value
gl_debug_linewidth1..10 (diagnostic, current session only)debug line width (pixels)
gl_depthbits0=auto / 16 / 24 / 32Requested depth buffer precision for the GL context. 0 = driver default. Startup/vid_restart cvar.
gl_dlight_falloff0..5Makes dynamic lights look a bit smoother, opposed to original jagged Quake 2 style. Default value is 1 (enabled).
gl_dotshading0/1/2Enables dotshading effect when drawing 3D models, which helps them look truly 3D-ish by simulating diffuse lighting from a fake light source. Default value is 1 (enabled).
gl_doublelight_entities0/1Specifies if combined modulation factor is applied to entity lighting one more time just before final lighting value is calculated, to simulate a well-known bug in the original Quake 2 renderer. Default value is 1 (apply twice). Entity lighting is calculated based on the color of the lightmap sample from the world surface directly beneath the entity. This means any cvar affecting lightmaps affects entity lighting as well (with exception of gl_modulate_world). Cvars that have effect only on the entity lighting are gl_modulate_entities and gl_doublelight_entities. Yet another cvar affecting entity lighting is gl_dotshading, which typically makes entities look a bit brighter. See also cl_noglow cvar which removes the pulsing effect (glowing) on bonus entities.
gl_downsample_skins0/1Specifies if skins are downsampled just like world textures are. When disabled, gl_round_down, gl_picmip cvars have no effect on skins. Default value is 1 (downsampling enabled).
gl_drawentities0/1draw model entities
gl_draworder0/1Alpha sorting treshold for transparent entitites. Entities with lower alpha are drawn in the front, while entities with higher alpha are drawn in the back. Default value is 1 (draw all entities in front).
gl_drawsky0/1Enables skybox texturing. 0 means to draw sky in solid black color. Default value is 1 (enabled).
gl_drawworld0/1draw world BSP
gl_dsa_paths0=legacy allocation / 1=auto (default) (diagnostic, current session only)Texture allocation path: OpenGL direct state access / immutable storage when the driver fully supports it, or the exact legacy allocation. The developer-only "force when available" mode is the session-only gl_dsa_paths_debug.
gl_dsa_paths_debugdefault 0 / 0=follow gl_dsa_paths / 1=force DSA fast paths when caps exist (session only) (diagnostic, current session only)Session-only diagnostic force for the OpenGL direct-state-access fast paths (gl_dsa_paths). 1 forces DSA mode 2 for this session: use the DSA/immutable-texture-storage paths whenever the driver capabilities exist, overriding the saved 0/1 production choice without rewriting it. Missing capabilities are never bypassed. A live console gl_dsa_paths 2 still enables it for the current session (legacy spelling); the persisted value stays the 0/1 baseline. Never read from a config and never written by any config or preset writer; after a restart it is off again.
gl_dynamic0=all dynamic lighting is disabled / 1=all dynamic lighting is enabled / 2=most dynamic lights are disabled, but lightmap updates are still allowed for switchable lights to workControls dynamic lightmap updates. Default value is 1.
gl_dynamic_alphadefault 0.20 / range 0..1 / step 0.05Alpha / opacity scale for the dynamic light contribution. Multiplies the final per-texel frac (and the per-entity f) by this factor before adding to the lightmap / entity color. 1.0 = legacy full intensity. Lower values make dlight projections more transparent / subtle on receiving surfaces — you can dial all dynamic lighting from full opaque (1.0) to invisible (0.0). Does not affect dlight existence, radius, or surface marking. Default 0.20 is the accepted soft blend.
gl_dynamic_dark_boostdefault 1.55 / range 0..10 / step 0.05Adaptive brightness boost for dynamic lights (blasters, rockets, explosions, lightning, flashlight engine fallback, etc.) on locally dark receivers. Inspects the static lightmap brightness at each receiving texel (and the AVFX celestial world multiplier when AVFX is on), and scales the per-dlight contribution up where the receiver is dark — so a blaster bolt next to a dark tunnel wall reads stronger, while the same bolt in a bright courtyard stays close to legacy. Also packs into the world shader's u_avfx_celestial_world.a slot so already-bright lightmap pixels (heavy dlight contribution OR static map lamps) get an anti-dim against the celestial multiplier — lets the dlight actually punch through AVFX night dimming. Independent of gl_dynamic: if gl_dynamic disables dynamic lights, this cvar does nothing. Does NOT touch radius, color, falloff, lightmap atlas, gl_modulate*, intensity, or AVFX celestial multipliers directly. Internal clamp on the per-texel boost is 1.0 .. 20.0. Set to 0 for byte-exact pre-1.4 behavior. Default 1.55 is balanced; crank up to 5..10 for dramatic cinematic effect.
gl_dynamic_radiusdefault 3.60 / range 0.2..10 / step 0.05Global radius scale for dynamic lights. Multiplies each dlight's effective intensity in the lightmap blocklight pass and in the per-entity light add. 1.0 = legacy. Values <1 shrink the projected glow on walls (blaster bolts make smaller spots). Values >1 stretch the glow within already-marked surfaces (the dlight cannot spread to NEW surfaces it didn't mark — that part of the engine runs earlier — but within the marked set the falloff curve extends further). Default 3.60 is the Q2PRO-X tuned dynamic-light radius.
gl_dynamic_softnessdefault 0.10 / range 0.1..5 / step 0.05Falloff softness for dynamic lights. Reshapes the linear frac/rad falloff (where 0 = at the dlight's radius edge, 1 = at its center) via pow(t, 1/softness). 1.0 = legacy linear. Values >1 = softer (brighter middle, more diffuse outer edge — like a flashlight's soft cone). Values <1 = harsher (concentrated pin-point bright core, sharp edge). Useful for tuning blaster/projectile glow shape without changing radius or intensity. Default 0.10 keeps the accepted crisp Q2PRO-X light shape.
gl_emissive_lightsdefault 0 / 0=off, 1=onMaster toggle for map-emissive local lighting. On map load Q2PRO-X scans visible, non-warp BSP SURF_LIGHT faces. Every light / light_* entry in the BSP entity lump is an invisible compiler marker and is rejected before both normal V_AddLight emission and AVFX material UBO generation. Accepted visible sources feed both paths. Selection is stable and has no camera-position term. The material path is gated by gl_dynamic and follows gl_dynamic_radius, gl_dynamic_softness, and gl_dynamic_alpha. Gameplay dlights keep priority. Raw player info_player_* origins are also excluded; gl_emissive_lights_spawn_points snaps starts to nearby support geometry. Optional gl_emissive_lights_pvs_gate is off by default.
gl_emissive_lights_dark_adaptdefault 1.0 / range 0.0..3.0 / step 0.05Reserved for E2: amplify emissive source strength on locally dark receivers, mirroring the gl_dynamic_dark_boost formula. Currently unused (E0+E1 landing reads the cvar value but does not apply it). Will activate in the E2 AVFX-material follow-up.
gl_emissive_lights_debugdefault 0 / 0=silent, 1=verbose (diagnostic, current session only)Diagnostics level for emissive map lights. 0 = silent; 1 = print cache-build summary at map load. Use emissive_lights_info command for on-demand diagnostics.
gl_emissive_lights_fade_msdefault 275 / range 0..1000 / step 25Activation fade time when the active source SET changes — e.g. when you toggle a sub-cvar (_surfaces / _entities / _spawn_points) or change _max_active. With stable B-prime selection, camera motion alone does NOT trigger fades because the same static source set wins every frame. Set to 0 for hard snap.
gl_emissive_lights_flickerdefault 0 / range 0.0..1.0 / step 0.01Lamp-like low-frequency flicker amplitude. 0 = stable lights. ~0.08 = subtle warm drift (like fluorescent ballast wobble). 1.0 = dramatic candle. Uses a stable per-source seed → no frame-to-frame buzzing. Default 0 keeps accepted map lamps stable.
gl_emissive_lights_intensitydefault 0.85 / range 0.0..5.0 / step 0.05Global intensity multiplier applied to every emissive source's base strength before flicker and per-frame budget selection. 0 disables emission entirely (cache stays built). 5 is dramatic.
gl_emissive_lights_max_activedefault 128 / range 0..128 / step 1Per-frame cap on emitted legacy V_AddLight emissive dlights. Gameplay (projectiles, muzzle flashes, sparks, explosions, flashlight) always wins the MAX_DLIGHTS slot race; emissive sources use leftovers. AVFX materials use separate static-emissive UBO families and are not limited by this value in the same way.
gl_emissive_lights_max_sourcesdefault 1024 / range 0..1024 / step 16Hard cap on the static source cache size built per map. 1024 is the accepted high-headroom default for dense maps. Lower values reduce per-frame selection work. 0 effectively disables emission (no sources cached).
gl_emissive_lights_pvs_gatedefault 0 / 0=no PVS gating (stable selection), 1=PVS gating (big-map mode)Optional PVS visibility gate (big-map/debug optimization). When 1, only sources whose origin cluster is in the camera PVS mask compete for the budget and material UBOs. This can save work on huge maps, but it can also make lights appear/disappear as the camera crosses cluster boundaries. Keep 0 for the stable always-on B-prime behavior.
gl_emissive_lights_rangedefault 320 / range 64..4096 / step 32Per-source range cap in world units. Each cached source has an intrinsic radius derived from BSP data; this cvar caps it so a single huge lamp can't light the whole map through walls. Lower values give tighter pools of light.
gl_emissive_lights_range_scaledefault 1.60 / range 0.1..4.0 / step 0.05Multiplier on each source's intrinsic radius BEFORE the global gl_emissive_lights_range cap. 1.60 = accepted tuned range. Lower values shrink ALL emissive ranges proportionally; higher values stretch them up to the cap.
gl_emissive_lights_spawn_pointsdefault 1 / 0=off, 1=snapped spawn-point / destination marker lightsSub-toggle for player spawn-point / destination marker lighting. This does NOT light the raw invisible info_player_* origin. Instead it snaps each player start to a nearby compact horizontal support surface and uses that geometry as the light source, so real spawn spots illuminate while unrelated wall lamps and stale arena-center pools are avoided. Texture names are not used. Also includes non-player destination markers such as misc_teleporter_dest.
gl_emissive_lights_surfacesdefault 0 / 0=ignore SURF_LIGHT faces, 1=use themSub-toggle: include visible BSP SURF_LIGHT faces in the emissive source cache. Accepted faces have a positive light value and are not SURF_SKY, SURF_NODRAW, or SURF_WARP; water is a receiver, never a lamp.
gl_finish0/1call glFinish each frame (latency test)
gl_flarespeed0=instant/no smooth fade / 8=default / higher=faster fadeSpecifies flare fading effect speed. Default value is 8 (0 = instant fade with no smooth interpolation, higher = faster fade). No code-side clamp beyond cvar parsing.
gl_fog0/1Enable re-release fog effect. Only effective when using GLSL backend. Default value is 1 (enabled).
gl_fontshadow0/1/2Specifies font shadow width, in pixels, ranging from 0 to 2. Default value is 0 (no shadow).
gl_gamma_scale_pics0/1Apply software gamma scaling not only to textures and skins, but to HUD pictures also. Default value is 0 (dont apply to pics).
gl_glowmap_intensity0..2Intensity factor for entity glowmaps. Default value is 0.75.
gl_gpu_timers0=off (default) / 1=on (diagnostic, current session only)Developer diagnostic: measure per-pass GPU time with non-blocking OpenGL timer queries (also switched on by the mirror benchmark). No GL work when off.
gl_gpulerp0=disabled / 1=auto (enabled on OpenGL 4.3 and higher) / 2=force enabledEnables alias model interpolation on GPU for potential rendering speedup. Default value is 1 (auto). If using OpenGL core profile, this option is always enabled. If not using GLSL backend, this option is always disabled.
gl_invert0/1Inverts colors of world textures. In combination with gl_saturation 0 effectively makes textures look like black and white photo negative. Default value is 0 (do not invert colors).
gl_lightgrid0/1use BSP lightgrid for entity lighting
gl_lightmap0=normal / 1=replace world textures with lightmaps / 2=also draw lightmap atlas overlay (debug build only; release acts as 1) (diagnostic, current session only)Lightmap visualization. 0 = normal render, 1 = replace world textures with lightmaps, 2 = also draw the lightmap atlas overlay (debug builds ONLY — Draw_Lightmaps() is gated under USE_DEBUG in main.c, so in release builds 2 behaves the same as 1).
gl_lightmap_bits0=auto / 7=128 / 8=256 / 9=512 / 10=1024Specifies size of lightmap textures as base-2 log of edge texel count. Default 0 = auto (typically 8 for regular maps, 10 for re-release maps). Code clamps non-zero to 7..10 → 128..1024 px. Older hardware may need adjustment for optimal dynamic lighting speed.
gl_lockpvs0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)freeze PVS at current position (debug)
gl_md5_distance0..16384Only use MD5 replacement model if entity is closer than this distance to the viewer, otherwise use original model. Default value is 2048. Setting this to 0 disables distance LOD.
gl_md5_load0/1Enables loading of MD5 replacement models as found in re-release. Default value is 1.
gl_md5_use0/1Enables use of MD5 replacement models as found in re-release. Only effective if gl_md5_load is enabled. Default value is 1.
gl_modulate0..4Specifies a primary modulation factor that each pixel of world lightmaps is multiplied by. This cvar affects entity lighting as well. Default value is 1 (identity).
gl_modulate_entities0..large multiplier, 1=identity/defaultSpecifies a secondary modulation factor that entity lighting is multiplied by. This cvar does not affect world lightmaps. Default value is 1 (identity). Multiplier, not boolean — typical 0..4 range, but any non-negative float.
gl_modulate_world0..large multiplier, 1=identity/defaultSpecifies a secondary modulation factor that each pixel of world lightmaps is multiplied by. This cvar does not affect entity lighting. Default value is 1 (identity). Multiplier, not boolean.
gl_multisamples0=off / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32Requested MSAA sample count for the GL context. 0 = no multisampling. Startup/vid_restart cvar.
gl_nobind0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)debug: skip texture binding
gl_noscrap0/1By default, OpenGL renderer combines small HUD pictures into the single texture called scrap. This usually speeds up rendering a bit, and allows pixel precise rendering of non power of two sized images. If you dont like this optimization for some reason, this cvar can be used to disable it. Default value is 0 (optimize).
gl_novbo0/1disable VBO usage
gl_novis0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)ignore PVS culling
gl_partscale0.25..8Specifies minimum size of particles. Default value is 2.
gl_partshape0=faded circle / 1=square / 2=fuller, less faded circleSpecifies shape of particles. Default value is 0.
gl_partstyle0=blend colors / 1=saturate colorsSpecifies drawing style of particles. Default value is 0.
gl_picmip0..31World-texture mip reduction level. Each +1 halves both upload dimensions; reduction stops independently for each texture at 1x1.
gl_polyblend0/1enable screen polyblend (damage/item pickup)
gl_post_contrast0.5..2post-process contrast
gl_post_profile0=off / 1=neutral / 2=warm / 3=arena / 4=cinematicPost-process colour-grading profile preset. Numeric integer 0..4; menu shows named labels but console uses numbers.
gl_post_temperature-1..1post-process colour temperature
gl_post_vibrance-1..1post-process vibrance
gl_postfx0/1 (master on/off)Master switch for post-process camera/display emulation effects (applied to the 3D scene only; HUD/menus stay crisp). 0 = off (no extra pass, identical to baseline). 1 = on; the effect is chosen by gl_postfx_mode. Works independently of HDR/bloom.
gl_postfx_crt_chroma0..1 (0 = none)CRT: horizontal chromatic aberration (RGB split). 0 = none.
gl_postfx_crt_curvature0..1 (0 = flat)CRT: screen curvature (barrel). Borders clamp/fade. 0 = flat.
gl_postfx_crt_flicker0..1 (0 = none)CRT: subtle temporal brightness flicker. 0 = none.
gl_postfx_crt_mask0..1 (0 = none)CRT: RGB phosphor aperture mask strength (per-column tint). 0 = none.
gl_postfx_crt_scanlines0..1 (0 = none)CRT: horizontal scanline darkening strength. 0 = none.
gl_postfx_crt_vignette0..1 (0 = none)CRT: darkening toward the screen edges. 0 = none.
gl_postfx_debug0 = off (diagnostic) (diagnostic, current session only)Diagnostic only (non-archived). Reserved for post-process debug visualization.
gl_postfx_film_chroma0..1 (0 = none)Film: subtle chromatic aberration. 0 = none.
gl_postfx_film_dirt0..1 (0 = none)Film: lens dirt/dust overlay. 0 = none.
gl_postfx_film_grain0..1 (0 = none)Film: animated grain amount. Deterministic, temporally controlled (not random snow).
gl_postfx_film_vignette0..1 (0 = none)Film: edge darkening. 0 = none.
gl_postfx_mix0..1 (1.0 = full effect)Blend of the effect with the normal (un-processed) image. 1.0 = full effect, 0.0 = no effect, 0.5 = half blend.
gl_postfx_mode0=off 1=pixel 2=crt 3=film 4=vhs 5=noir 6=sepiaActive post-process effect when gl_postfx 1. 0 = off, 1 = Pixel Retro (pixelation + color posterize), 2 = CRT (scanlines/mask/vignette/chroma), 3 = Film (grain + vignette), 4 = VHS (jitter + chroma bleed + noise), 5 = Noir (black & white + contrast), 6 = Sepia.
gl_postfx_pixel_dither0/1 (0 = off)Pixel Retro: ordered 4x4 dithering to soften posterize banding. 0 = off.
gl_postfx_pixel_filter0=nearest 1=softenedPixel Retro: 0 = nearest (hard pixels), 1 = softened sampling.
gl_postfx_pixel_grid0..1 (0 = no grid)Pixel Retro: visible grid/gap between virtual pixels (retro LCD look). 0 = none.
gl_postfx_pixel_levels2..64 (fewer = stronger posterize)Pixel Retro: number of color quantization levels per channel (posterize). 2 = harsh, 16 = mild, 64 = subtle.
gl_postfx_pixel_palette0/1 (0 = off)Pixel Retro: snap colors to a fixed 16-color retro palette. 0 = off.
gl_postfx_pixel_virtual_y120..1080 (lower = chunkier)Pixel Retro: virtual vertical resolution the scene is quantized to. Lower = chunkier pixels (e.g. 120), higher = finer (e.g. 480). The grid is stable under camera/player movement.
gl_postfx_strength0..2 (1.0 = nominal)Overall intensity of the active post-process effect. 1.0 = nominal. Also drives Film grain and VHS noise/jitter/chroma intensity.
gl_postfx_vhs_chroma_bleed0..1 (0 = none)VHS: horizontal color bleed/smear. 0 = none.
gl_postfx_vhs_jitter0..1 (0 = none)VHS: per-scanline horizontal jitter. 0 = none.
gl_postfx_vhs_noise0..1 (0 = none)VHS: analog noise amount. 0 = none.
gl_postfx_vhs_tracking0..1 (0 = none)VHS: vertical tracking distortion band. 0 = none.
gl_print_capabilitiesdefault 1 / 0=silent, 1=print at startupPrint a single self-contained block to the console + log at engine startup describing the detected GL profile, GLSL version, framebuffer pixel format, and per-capability QGL_CAP_* yes/no plus the chosen AVFX real celestial sphere tier. Block content: GL_VENDOR / GL_RENDERER / GL_VERSION / GL_SHADING_LANGUAGE_VERSION (raw driver strings), detected profile (OpenGL ES X.Y or OpenGL (Desktop) X.Y) with parsed major.minor + parsed GLSL major.minor, max texture / renderbuffer / viewport size, color / Z / stencil bit depths, pipeline class (programmable shaders vs fixed-function, legacy compat flag), per-capability rows for QGL_CAP_SHADER_STORAGE (SSBO; GLES 3.1+ / OpenGL 4.3+), QGL_CAP_BUFFER_TEXTURE (skeletal mesh upload), QGL_CAP_INSTANCING (AVFX snow / foam / dust / visualfx instancing), QGL_CAP_TEXTURE_ANISOTROPY, QGL_CAP_TEXTURE_CLAMP_TO_EDGE, QGL_CAP_NON_POWER_OF_TWO, QGL_CAP_ELEMENT_INDEX_UINT, QGL_CAP_CLIENT_VA (legacy vertex arrays), and a final AVFX real celestial tier: line with the chosen tier name and star / line caps (SSBO fragment-safe cap 256/674, UBO fallback 128/160, Classic 56/27). Default 1 so the block is visible on every start without a +set line. Set to 0 to silence the startup block (the value persists via CVAR_ARCHIVE). The console command gl_capabilities reprints the same block on demand regardless of this cvar. Independent of gl_strings (legacy strings command), which prints a narrower three-line summary plus the extension list.
gl_profileempty=highest compatibility/default / gl=OpenGL core default / gl3.2 / gl4.6 / es=OpenGL ES default / es3.0 / (startup/vid_restart)Specifies custom profile and version of OpenGL context to create. Default empty = highest compatibility profile available. "gl" = core profile, "es" = OpenGL ES, optionally followed by minimum version ("gl3.2", "gl4.6", "es3.0"). Not all drivers support every value. Startup/vid_restart cvar.
gl_render_scale100..1000 (percent; 100 = native, 200 = 2x super-sampling, etc.; menu step 1%)Internal 3D scene resolution as a percent of the display. 100 is native resolution; >100 is super-sampling (render higher, downscale for AA); <100 is not supported — set gl_render_scale to 100 to disable super-sampling. Runtime-clamped by gl_render_scale_max and the backend's max texture size. Menu step 1% (was 25% — 1% gives finer control on the SS curve).
gl_render_scale_applied100..1000 (read-only; check after setting gl_render_scale)Read-only diagnostic: the render scale that was actually applied on the last frame after all clamps (max, backend limits, fallback). Useful when the requested value was clipped and you need to know the effective resolution.
gl_render_scale_filter0=fast single blit / 1=balanced progressive 2x / 2=quality progressive 2x + tiled guard bandRender scale upscale / downscale filter quality. Integer 0..2. 0 = single fast blit (cheap, slight blur). 1 = balanced progressive 2x downsample chain. 2 = quality progressive 2x + tiled-mode guard band (sharpest, most VRAM/perf).
gl_render_scale_max100..1000 (percent)Maximum render scale clamp. The engine will never exceed this even if gl_render_scale is set higher — protects against accidentally setting 1000% on a 4K display and running out of VRAM.
gl_render_scale_mode0=auto / 1=texture/FBO / 2=blit / 3=tiledRender scale pipeline mode. Integer 0..3. 0 = auto pick. 1 = render into offscreen texture / FBO (preferred for >100% SSAA). 2 = direct blit path when supported. 3 = tiled mode for very high render scales that exceed max texture size.
gl_render_scale_pathdirect / texture / blit / tiled (read-only effective path)Read-only effective render scale path actually in use after gl_render_scale_mode applies (auto resolves to a concrete path here). Useful diagnostic — tells you whether the renderer is in direct, texture, blit, or tiled mode right now.
gl_round_down0/1round texture sizes down to power of 2
gl_saturation0=grayscale / 1=original colourEnables grayscaling of world textures. 1 keeps original colors, 0 converts textures to grayscale (saves video memory and speeds up rendering since textures upload at 8 bpp instead of 24). Any value in between reduces colourfulness. Default 1. Code clamps to 0..1.
gl_shader_binary_cachedefault 1 / 0=always compile from source, 1=load/save program binariesPersistent OpenGL program-binary cache. When supported (GL_ARB_get_program_binary / GLES 3.0+), each successfully linked GL program — both stock state-bit permutations and the dedicated AVFX pass programs (stars / meteors / comets / impacts) — is saved to baseq2/q2pro-x/shcache/<digest>.bin and reloaded on later runs, skipping GLSL compile+link. The digest folds GL vendor/renderer/version, backend/API tier, storage tier and the shader source hashes, so a binary is never loaded under an incompatible driver/backend; a stale or rejected binary is deleted and the program is recompiled from source (never a black screen). Works together with gl_shader_prewarm: the prewarm pass loads binaries instead of compiling on warm runs. Default 1. See shader_cache_info / shader_cache_clear.
gl_shader_binary_cache_writedefault 1 / 0=read-only (no new files), 1=write new binariesWrite sub-switch for gl_shader_binary_cache. When 1, newly compiled program binaries are written to baseq2/q2pro-x/shcache. Set to 0 to use the existing cache read-only — warm hits still load, but no new files are added (useful after the cache is fully populated, or on a read-only install). Default 1. Has no effect when gl_shader_binary_cache is 0 or program-binary support is absent.
gl_shader_compile_threadsdefault -1 / -1=safe CPU-scaled auto (driver max only in Aggressive), 0=none, N=fixedBackground shader-compiler thread count requested when gl_shader_parallel_compile is active. -1 Auto (default) = half the logical CPUs capped at 8 in normal EGL Auto; with Aggressive mode it requests the implementation maximum. 0 = request no background compiler threads. N = request exactly N threads. Only meaningful on a supporting backend. The requested value and the GL state are shown by shader_prewarm_info.
gl_shader_parallel_compiledefault 1 / 0=serial, 1=safe CPU-scaled EGL auto, 2=aggressive overrideParallel shader-compile hint. When the GL backend exposes GL_ARB/KHR_parallel_shader_compile, the prewarm pass may compile/link programs on background threads, shortening a cold map-load compile. 0 Off = serial. 1 Auto (default) keeps native WGL serial and uses a bounded CPU-scaled EGL pool: half the logical CPUs, capped at 8. 2 Aggressive permits the implementation maximum when gl_shader_compile_threads is Auto, or the exact configured count. No effect without the extension. shader_prewarm_info reports the requested pool and queue. Warm runs load cached binaries.
gl_shader_parallel_inflightdefault 0 (auto) / 0=twice the safe pool (2..16), 1..64=explicit in-flight capMaximum async shader programs queued at once during prewarm. 0 Auto (default) = twice the safe compiler-pool size, clamped to 2..16. N = an explicit cap, clamped 1..64. The bounded Auto queue keeps compiler workers fed without retaining dozens of heavy AVFX programs in ANGLE simultaneously. Explicit larger queues remain available for Aggressive tuning. shader_prewarm_info shows inflight_cap_resolved / peak_inflight.
gl_shader_prewarm0 Off, 1 Auto (default: AVFX or HDR), 2 AlwaysShader prewarm POLICY (3-state, TZ 2026-06-05; was a boolean toggle). 0 Off = never auto-run the forced map-load / first-frame shader prewarm. 1 Auto (default) = run when the session needs it: cl_avfx is on OR a non-AVFX renderer feature such as HDR (gl_hdr) is effective (HDR-1 added — the HDR tone-map composite must be prewarmed too); unaffected players get no forced prewarm and no 'Loading shaders...' phase. 2 Always = run even with everything off (stock/world/postprocess keys only), preserving the old aggressive behaviour for diagnostics. See gl_shader_prewarm_avfx for the AVFX include/exclude sub-gate; shader_prewarm_info shows the live policy and last skip reason.
gl_shader_prewarm_progressdefault 1 / 0=no progress UI, 1=show shader compile/cache-load progressShow a visible progress indicator while shaders compile or load from the binary cache during a cold map load, so the client never looks frozen. The diagnostic counters (last total / updates / elapsed_ms) are visible via shader_prewarm_info regardless of this toggle. Default 1.
gl_shader_prewarm_verbosedefault 0 / 0=silent, 1=print stats after each prewarm run (diagnostic, current session only)Per-run prewarm diagnostics to console: reason (map_load / viewport_change / cvar_change / manual), attempted, compiled_new, already_cached, failed, time_ms, longest_program_us. Same numbers are always available on demand via the shader_prewarm_info console command. Default 0 keeps the console quiet.
gl_shader_variant_warmupdefault 1 / 0=off, 1=auto (accepted), 2=aggressiveProduction draw-variant warmup. Some ANGLE/D3D backends only materialise a shader's true draw-time output-layout variant on the FIRST real production draw, even when compile/link prewarm already finished (compiled_from_src=0) — so the first map can still stutter. This warms those variants with a tiny scoped real BSP sky/water draw (scissored to a few pixels, refdef/viewport restored) plus a post-draw binary save under the effective shader key, so the variant is cached. 0 Off = skip. 1 Auto (default) = the accepted behaviour. 2 Aggressive = widen coverage. No effect when cl_avfx is 0. shader_prewarm_info shows production_variant_warmup mode + warmed face counts.
gl_shaders0/1Enables GLSL rendering backend (OpenGL 3.0+). Disabling is rejected while shader-dependent features are enabled: tessellation, AVFX, HDR/output, bloom, post-processing, render scale above 100%, fog, cubemaps or glowmaps. The console lists enabled blockers in red; the current value is preserved. These features also cannot be enabled with gl_shaders 0. Default 1.
gl_shadows0=disabled / 1=hard, constant alpha / 2=hard, alpha fade with distance / 3=soft, alpha fade with distanceControls projected shadows underneath 3D models. Mode 3 uses a softer non-stencil shadow pass. Default value is 0.
gl_shadows_light_occlusiondefault 1 / 0=legacy gl_shadows always, 1=require open light path overheadSuppress legacy projected model shadows (gl_shadows) when the model is under a solid ceiling with no overhead light path. After all existing cull_shadow rejection tests pass, traces 5 sample points (center + 4 cardinal offsets at clamp(radius × 0.35, 4, 48) wu) straight up by 8192 wu through the loaded BSP. Any sample that reaches a SURF_SKY brush or escapes the world (fraction=1.0) allows the shadow; if all 5 hit solid non-sky geometry, the shadow is suppressed. Independent from the accepted AVFX flashlight dynamic GPU shadows — those run their own shadow-map pass and are NOT touched by this gate. Set to 0 to restore exact legacy gl_shadows behavior. Default 1 because this is a correctness fix for the new 1.4 lighting model (it stops fake floor decals from appearing under closed ceilings in dark indoor scenes).
gl_sharpen0..1sharpen post-process amount
gl_showbloom0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)debug: visualize bloom buffer
gl_showerrors0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)print GL errors each frame
gl_showorigins0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)draw entity origin markers
gl_showscrap0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)debug: visualize scrap atlas
gl_showstats0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)print render statistics each frame
gl_showtearing0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)debug: draw tearing bar
gl_showtris0=off / 1=world / 2=models / 4=2D pics / 8=effects (bitmask, combine by sum) (diagnostic, current session only)Bitmask debug overlay: draw triangle wireframe over various render groups. Combine flags by sum (e.g. 3 = world + models, 15 = all).
gl_stencilbits0=off / 8Requested stencil buffer bits for the GL context. Mostly used for stencil shadows (gl_shadows). Startup/vid_restart cvar.
gl_swapinterval-1/0/1swap interval (VSync)
gl_testint (diagnostic, current session only)generic test cvar (debug)
gl_texturebits0=driver/default / 1..8=low precision / 9..16=16-bit-ish / 17+=8-bit/channel; common values 0,8,16,32Specifies bits per texel for internal texture storage. Default 0 = driver default. Common values 0, 8, 16, 32.
gl_texturemodeGL_NEAREST / GL_LINEAR / GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST / GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_NEAREST / GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR / GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR / MAG_NEARESTOpenGL texture filter mode for world textures and model skins (IT_WALL, IT_SKIN). Does not control HUD pictures, fonts, or skyboxes (those use gl_bilerp_pics, gl_bilerp_chars, gl_bilerp_skies). Whitelist of GL filter strings; menu labels like "nearest" / "trilinear" are NOT accepted on the console. Related: gl_anisotropy. Default GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR.
gl_upscale_pcx0=dont upscale / 1=upscale 2x (takes 5x more memory) / 2=upscale 4x (takes 21x more memory)Enables upscaling of PCX images using HQ2x and HQ4x filters. This improves rendering quality when screen scaling is used. Default value is 0.
gl_vertexlight0/1per-vertex lighting (retro)
gl_vis_overlay_lite0=normal / 1=strip fog / 2=strip glowmap / 4=strip bloom MRT writes / 8=skip cel-shading edge pass / 16=white texture on tint pass / 31=all diagnostic strips (bitmask) (diagnostic, current session only)Diagnostic bitmask for stripping render passes from the Option O vis-overlay path. Runtime debug only — not a graphics-quality knob, not archived. Combine flags by sum (e.g. 5 = strip fog + bloom MRT writes).
gl_waterwarp0/1Enable screen warping effect when underwater. Only effective when using GLSL backend. Default value is 0 (disabled).
gl_znear0.5..16 typical, default 2GL near clip plane (world units). Default 2. Smaller values render closer geometry but reduce z-buffer precision at distance.
r_diag_present0=off (default) / 1=on (diagnostic, current session only)Developer diagnostic: high-resolution timing of the frame present (swap) step.
r_frame_spike_threshold_msmilliseconds (default 25) (diagnostic, current session only)Frame spike detector: a frame longer than this is recorded; frame_spike_info prints the spikes, frame_spike_reset clears them.
r_fullbright0/1 (diagnostic, current session only)render world fullbright
r_glowmaps0/1Enables loading of glowmap images as found in re-release. Only effective if gl_shaders is enabled. Default value is 1.
r_maxfps0..1000Specifies maximum rendering frame rate if cl_async is set to 1, otherwise ignored. Default value is 0, which means no particular limit.
r_override_textures0=dont override textures / 1=override only palettized textures / 2=override all texturesEnables automatic overriding of palettized textures (in WAL or PCX format) with truecolor replacements (in PNG, JPG or TGA format) by stripping off original file extension and searching for alternative filenames in the order specified by r_texture_formats variable. Default value is 1.
r_texture_formatsstringSpecifies the order in which truecolor texture replacements are searched. Default value is "png jpg tga".
r_texture_overrides1=HUD pictures / 2=HUD fonts / 4=skins / 8=sprites / 16=wall textures / 32=sky texturesSpecifies what types of textures are affected by r_override_textures. This variable is a bitmask. Default value is -1 (all types).
r_vis_overlay_debug_modedefault 0 / 0=off, >0=mode (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: visibility-overlay renderer debug mode. 0=off. Not archived, no menu; zero cost at 0.
r_vis_overlay_isolate0=instanced (default) / 1=single draws (diagnostic, current session only)Developer diagnostic: draw each visibility overlay through the single-draw path instead of the instanced pipeline (to reproduce overlay flicker without instancing).
r_vis_overlay_quality_fuse0=separate passes / 1=fused (default) (diagnostic, current session only)Visibility overlays: fuse the quality passes into one (the faster path). 0 is kept for A/B comparison.
vid_activation_debugdefault 0 / 0=no live activation/sync lines / 1=print them (diagnostic, current session only)Live console diagnostics for window activation and client sync mode. 0 (default) prints no spontaneous "window activation:" or "sync mode:" lines and costs nothing: the activation logger returns before it even queries the foreground window. 1 enables both live lines in their original format. The sync-transition ring keeps recording either way, so the explicit cl_sync_info command still reports recent transitions while this is off. Session-only: never written to a config or a preset, and absent from the guided menus.
vid_debug_fail_first_initdefault 0 / 0=off, 1=fail the first driver once (diagnostic, current session only)Developer-only: tear the primary video driver down after a successful init to exercise the real fallback path (Win32 lifecycle fixture). One-shot: consumed on use, session-only. 0=off; zero cost at 0.
vid_desktop_fullscreen0=exclusive fullscreen / 1=desktop fullscreen (default)Fullscreen as a borderless window at the desktop mode (fast Alt-Tab) instead of an exclusive video mode change.
vid_desktop_fullscreen_fit0=fill (default) / 1=aspectDesktop fullscreen: stretch the picture to the monitor, or keep the selected mode's aspect with black bars.
vid_desktop_fullscreen_margin-1=exact size (default) / 0=fast Alt-Tab on deep-color WGL / 1..16=manual diagnostic marginDesktop-fullscreen Alt-Tab policy. Default -1 uses the exact monitor size and preserves maximum native-WGL FPS, but Alt-Tab can be slower on desktops deeper than 8 bpc. Value 0 enables automatic fast-Alt-Tab compatibility: deep-color SDR WGL leaves a minimal right-edge margin to avoid Legacy Flip, potentially at an FPS cost. Active FP16 true HDR remains exact-size. Positive values are manual diagnostic margins. Requires vid_restart.
vid_desktop_fullscreen_margin_debugdefault 0 / 0=follow vid_desktop_fullscreen_margin / >0=manual margin in pixels (session only) (diagnostic, current session only)Session-only manual margin for desktop fullscreen (vid_desktop_fullscreen_margin). A positive value shrinks the borderless desktop-fullscreen window by that many pixels for this session only, overriding the stable persisted policy (-1 exact size, 0 automatic fast-Alt-Tab compatibility) without rewriting it. Used to diagnose presentation/compositor behaviour at non-exact window sizes. A startup vid_desktop_fullscreen_margin <positive> outside a config is migrated here automatically. Never read from a config and never written by any config or preset writer; after a restart it is off again.
vid_display_gammadefault 1 / range 0.3..3 / step 0.05 / liveOptional live final-composite gamma for programmable WGL/EGL. Default 1.0 is neutral; lower values brighten the complete frame and higher values darken it. This new control is deliberately independent from legacy vid_gamma and never inherits its persisted value. Owned by the unified global video config when global video preferences are enabled.
vid_driverwin32wgl=Windows WGL OpenGL (default, fast cold AVFX startup) / win32egl=Windows EGL/ANGLE (explicit capture/true-HDR choice) / wayland=native Wayland / x11=native X11 / sdl=SDL2Specifies which video driver to use. On Windows the default is win32wgl: native OpenGL has the fast cold AVFX startup path. win32egl remains an explicit capture-friendly ANGLE choice for NVIDIA ShadowPlay/OBS compatibility and is required for the optional true-HDR output path, but its first cold shader build can take much longer. If the chosen backend fails to initialize the engine probes the remaining drivers and rewrites vid_driver to the backend that actually started.
vid_flip_on_switch0=off (default) / 1=onRestore the desktop video mode when you switch away from an exclusive fullscreen game (Windows).
vid_force_foreground_on_start0=off (default) / 1=activate once / 2=test keepaliveRuntime-only agent-test switch. 1 activates Q2PRO-X once after the menu/map is presented; 2 keeps the test process foreground for its lifetime. Command-line only and never saved.
vid_fullscreen0/1/2If set to non zero _value_, run in the specified fullscreen mode. This way, _value_ acts as index into the list of video modes specified by vid_modelist. Default value is 0, which means to run in windowed mode.
vid_fullscreen_typedesktop=Desktop fullscreen / exclusive=Exclusive fullscreenBorderless desktop vs classic exclusive mode.
vid_gammadefault 1 / range 0.3..3 / step 0.05 / r_reload/vid_restartCompatibility texture gamma used by existing Q2/Q2PRO configs. Default 1.0 = identity; lower values brighten texture mid-tones, higher values darken them. On programmable WGL/EGL it is baked into wall/skin texture uploads and therefore needs r_reload or vid_restart; it never changes the whole final frame. With vid_hwgamma 1, the display backend may instead consume this curve as a hardware gamma ramp. Owned by the unified global video config when global video preferences are enabled.
vid_geometrystringSize and optional position of the main window on virtual desktop. Full syntax is: WxH[+X+Y]. Default value is "640x480".
vid_hwgammadefault 0 / 0/1 / vid_restartApply the legacy vid_gamma curve as a hardware gamma ramp through the display driver instead of baking it into textures. Default 0 = off; 1 = on. Registered as CVAR_REFRESH, so enabling it needs vid_restart and driver support; once active, changes to vid_gamma are live. Independent from the optional final-composite vid_display_gamma. Owned by the unified global video config when global video preferences are enabled.
vid_modeliststringSpace separated list of fullscreen video modes. Both _freq_ and _bpp_ parameters are optional. Full syntax is: WxH[@freq][:bpp] [...]. Default value is "640x480 800x600 1024x768". On Linux, _freq_ parameter is currently ignored. Special keyword desktop means to use default desktop video mode.
vid_refgl/softrenderer backend
vid_refreshmax / rate in Hz from vid_refresh_list / emptyFullscreen refresh rate picked from vid_refresh_list. max = the highest available; ignored in windowed and desktop fullscreen modes.
vid_refresh_listlist (read-only)Read-only list of the refresh rates available for the selected resolution, for vid_refresh.
vid_resolutiondesktop / WIDTHxHEIGHT from vid_resolution_list / emptyFullscreen resolution picked from the list the monitor reports (vid_resolution_list). desktop = the monitor's native mode; empty = the legacy vid_modelist / vid_fullscreen choice.
vid_resolution_listlist (read-only)Read-only list of the fullscreen resolutions the monitor reports, for vid_resolution.
vid_test_no_activate0=normal (default) / 1=never activate (diagnostic, current session only)Test-harness switch: never bring the game window to the foreground or take focus. Set on the command line by automated checks.
vid_windowed0=off / 1=onvid_windowed: run in a window instead of fullscreen.

HDR, screenshots and display protection

Variables in this section: 47.

VariableAccepted valuesDescription
gl_hdr0=off / LDR (default) / 1=auto (HDR when supported) / 2=force (developer)Master switch for the optional HDR / tone-mapping render pipeline. Off keeps the accepted LDR look exactly. Auto enables HDR scene rendering when the backend can actually render to a floating-point scene buffer (probed at startup — see gl_hdr_info). Force is a developer setting that requests HDR even on marginal backends.
